fr.B: Un homme de la foule {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répondit : « Maître, je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ai amené mon fils. Il a un esprit qui l’empêche de parler.
fr.R: Un homme dans la foule a répondu : « Maître, je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ai amené mon fils. Il y a en lui un esprit mauvais qui l’empêche de parler.

sw.L: Na mtu mmoja katika umati akamjibu, "Mwalimu, nimemleta mwanangu {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}}, [kwa sababu] ana pepo bubu;
sw.B: Mtu mmoja katika umati akamjibu, "Mwalimu, nimemleta mwanangu {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}}. Ana pepo anayemfanya asiweze kusema.
sw.R: Mtu mmoja katika umati akajibu, "Mwalimu, nimemleta mwanangu {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}}. Ana pepo mbaya ndani yake, anayemzuia asiseme.

pt.L: E um da multidão {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} respondeu: "Mestre, eu trouxe o meu filho a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, [pois ele] tem um espírito mudo;
pt.B: Um homem da multidão {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} respondeu: "Mestre, eu trouxe o meu filho até {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}. Ele tem um espírito que o deixa sem fala.
pt.R: Um homem da multidão respondeu: "Mestre, eu trouxe o meu filho até {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}. Há um espírito mau nele que não o deixa falar.

decisions.choice: a mute spirit: a spirit that keeps him from speaking
alternatives: a spirit that does not speak
decisions.reason: The spirit is named by what it does to the boy. In 9:25 it is also called deaf.

decisions.choice: I brought my son to you: he came looking for Jesus
alternatives: he brought him to the disciples
decisions.reason: Jesus was on the mountain, so the father asked the disciples instead (9:18).

decisions.choice: one of the crowd: the man is not named
decisions.reason: He is simply a man in the crowd, a father (9:21).

decisions.choice: an evil spirit
decisions.reason: Readable uses "evil spirit", as in earlier chapters, and says what the spirit does.

decisions.choice: the father says "Thưa Thầy" and "Thầy" for "you", "tôi" for himself, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: He comes to Jesus as to a respected teacher, as the Greek "Teacher" says.

decisions.choice: "linh câm" (L); "một linh làm cho câm" (B); "tà linh" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the short Greek phrase; Balanced says what the spirit does; Readable calls it an evil spirit, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "말 못 하게 하는 영" (L, B); "악한 영" (R)
decisions.reason: The mute spirit is one that keeps the boy from speaking (meaning decision); "벙어리" is now felt as a slur on people who cannot speak. Readable says "악한 영" as Mark 3 does for spirits.

decisions.choice: espíritu maligno
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says what kind of spirit it is. The same words stand for "unclean spirit" at Readable (9:25).

decisions.choice: Maître
decisions.reason: The Greek word means "Teacher". "Maître" is the French word for a teacher who has disciples, as in the French John (1:38); "enseignant" and "professeur" sound like a school. Used the same way in 9:38.

decisions.choice: pepo, with personal agreement (pepo bubu anayemfanya); pepo mbaya (R)
alternatives: pepo with the agreement of a thing (pepo inayomfanya)
decisions.reason: The spirit acts as a person in this story (it sees Jesus, shrieks, is commanded), so it takes the agreement of a living being, as in Mark 1:23 and 5:2. "Pepo", as for the unclean spirits throughout Mark; "roho" is kept for the Holy Spirit and the human spirit. Readable says "pepo mbaya" (evil spirit), as the English Readable does and as the earlier chapters do. For review by a native speaker.

decisions.choice: a ti, até ti
decisions.reason: The father speaks to Jesus, so he says "tu" (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4), here and in 9:18 ("teus discípulos") and 9:22 ("se tu podes", "tem compaixão").

source.text: καὶ ὅπου ἐὰν αὐτὸν καταλάβῃ ῥήσσει αὐτόν, καὶ ἀφρίζει καὶ τρίζει τοὺς ὀδόντας καὶ ξηραίνεται· καὶ εἶπα τοῖς μαθηταῖς σου ἵνα αὐτὸ ἐκβάλωσιν, καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσαν.

records.literal_gloss: and whenever if him it seizes, it throws down him, and he foams and gnashes the teeth and is withering; and I spoke to the disciples of you that it they might cast out, and not they had power.

en.L: and wherever it seizes him, it throws him down, and he foams and grinds [his] teeth and becomes rigid; and I told {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples to cast it out, and they were not able."
en.B: Whenever it takes hold of him, it dashes him to the ground, and he foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth, and goes stiff. I asked {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples to throw it out, but they did not have the strength."
en.R: Whenever the spirit takes control of him, it throws him to the ground. Foam comes out of his mouth, he grinds his teeth, and his body becomes stiff. I asked {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} followers to force the spirit out, but they could not do it."

vi.L: và hễ ở đâu nó nhập vào cháu, thì nó vật cháu xuống, và cháu sùi bọt, nghiến răng, rồi trở nên cứng đờ; và tôi đã nói với các môn đồ của Thầy để họ đuổi nó ra, nhưng họ không đủ sức."
vi.B: Hễ nó nhập vào cháu thì nó vật cháu ngã xuống đất, cháu sùi bọt mép, nghiến răng, rồi cứng đờ người. Tôi đã xin các môn đồ của Thầy đuổi nó ra, nhưng họ không đủ sức."
vi.R: Mỗi khi tà linh ấy nhập vào cháu, nó vật cháu xuống đất. Miệng cháu sùi bọt, cháu nghiến răng, và cả người cháu cứng đờ. Tôi đã xin các môn đồ của Thầy đuổi tà linh ra, nhưng họ không làm được."

ko.L: 그 [영이] 어디서든지 그를 사로잡으면, 그를 거꾸러뜨립니다. 그러면 그는 거품을 흘리고 이를 갈며 몸이 뻣뻣해집니다. 그래서 제가 선생님의 제자들에게 그것을 쫓아내 달라고 말했는데, 그들은 할 수 없었습니다."
ko.B: 그 영이 아이를 사로잡기만 하면 땅에 거꾸러뜨립니다. 그러면 아이는 입에 거품을 물고 이를 갈며 몸이 뻣뻣해집니다. 그래서 선생님의 제자들에게 그 영을 쫓아내 달라고 했는데, 그들은 쫓아낼 힘이 없었습니다."
ko.R: 그 영이 아이를 붙잡으면 언제든지 아이를 땅바닥에 내던집니다. 아이는 입에서 거품을 흘리고 이를 갈며 온몸이 뻣뻣해집니다. 그래서 선생님의 제자들에게 그 영을 쫓아내 달라고 했는데, 그들은 하지 못했습니다."

es.L: y dondequiera que se apodera de él, lo derriba, y echa espuma y rechina los dientes y se queda rígido; y les dije a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} discípulos que lo expulsaran, y no pudieron».
es.B: Cada vez que se apodera de él, lo tira al suelo, y él echa espuma por la boca, rechina los dientes y se queda rígido. Les pedí a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} discípulos que lo expulsaran, pero no tuvieron fuerza para hacerlo».
es.R: Cada vez que el espíritu se apodera de él, lo tira al suelo. Le sale espuma por la boca, rechina los dientes y su cuerpo se pone rígido. Les pedí a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} discípulos que hicieran salir al espíritu, pero no pudieron».

fr.L: et partout où il le saisit, il le jette à terre, et il écume, et il grince des dents, et il devient raide ; et j’ai dit à {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} disciples de le chasser, et ils n’en ont pas eu la force. »
fr.B: Chaque fois que l’esprit s’empare de lui, il le jette à terre ; alors il a de l’écume à la bouche, il grince des dents et il devient tout raide. J’ai demandé à {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} disciples de le chasser, mais ils n’en ont pas eu la force. »
fr.R: Chaque fois que l’esprit le prend, il le jette par terre. De l’écume sort de sa bouche, il grince des dents et son corps devient tout raide. J’ai demandé à {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} disciples de chasser l’esprit, mais ils n’ont pas pu. »

sw.L: na popote anapomkamata, humwangusha chini, naye hutoa povu na kusaga meno na kukakamaa; na nikawaambia wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wamtoe, lakini hawakuweza."
sw.B: Kila anapomshika, humwangusha chini kwa nguvu, naye hutokwa na povu kinywani, husaga meno na kukakamaa mwili. Niliwaomba wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wamfukuze, lakini hawakuwa na nguvu ya kufanya hivyo."
sw.R: Kila pepo huyo anapomshika, humwangusha chini. Povu hutoka kinywani mwake, husaga meno, na mwili wake hukakamaa. Niliwaomba wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wamtoe pepo huyo, lakini hawakuweza."

pt.L: e, onde quer que ele o agarre, o derruba, e ele espuma, e range os dentes, e fica rígido; e eu disse aos {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} discípulos que o expulsassem, e eles não tiveram força."
pt.B: Sempre que o espírito o domina, joga o menino no chão, e ele espuma pela boca, range os dentes e fica todo duro. Pedi aos {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} discípulos que o expulsassem, mas eles não tiveram força para isso."
pt.R: Toda vez que o espírito toma conta dele, joga o menino no chão. Sai espuma da boca dele, ele range os dentes e o corpo dele fica duro. Eu pedi aos {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} seguidores que mandassem o espírito embora, mas eles não conseguiram."

decisions.choice: becomes rigid: goes stiff during the attack
decisions.reason: The verb means to dry up or wither. In this list of what happens in an attack it most likely means the body goes stiff. It could mean he is wasting away.

decisions.choice: the attacks: like what is now called an epileptic seizure
decisions.reason: The signs are those of a seizure. Mark tells it as the work of a spirit, and Jesus deals with it as one (9:25). Matthew 17:15 also describes the boy's fits.

decisions.choice: wherever: at any place and time
decisions.reason: The word means where, but with "if" it covers every occasion.

decisions.choice: they were not able: they lacked the strength
decisions.reason: The verb means to have strength. The disciples had driven out spirits before (6:13) but failed here.

decisions.choice: foams at the mouth (B); foam comes out of his mouth (R)
decisions.reason: English needs "mouth" with this verb.

decisions.choice: "cháu" for the boy in his father's words; "nó" for the spirit
decisions.reason: A Vietnamese parent speaking to a respected person calls his own child "cháu"; keeping "nó" for the spirit also keeps the two apart, which the Greek pronouns leave to the context.

decisions.choice: "môn đồ" at every level, Readable included
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese guide keeps "môn đồ" at every level, where the English Readable says "followers"; the same through Mark 9-10.

decisions.choice: "đuổi ... ra" for casting out a spirit, at every level
decisions.reason: The ordinary word for driving out a spirit; the same in 9:28 and 9:38.

decisions.choice: [영이]
decisions.reason: The Greek verb has no stated subject; Korean needs one, and Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: expulsar (L, B); hacer salir (R)
decisions.reason: The verb Mark uses for driving out demons. "Expulsar" is the plain Spanish word; Readable says it more simply, as the English "force out" does.

decisions.choice: disciples (R)
alternatives: ceux qui te suivent (R), as the English Readable says "followers"
decisions.reason: The French guide keeps "disciples" at every level, Readable included: the word is plain French and recurs through the Gospel. Used the same way in the whole chapter.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτοῖς λέγει· Ὦ γενεὰ ἄπιστος, ἕως πότε πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἔσομαι;

records.literal_gloss: And answering them he says, O generation unbelieving, until when with you will I be?

en.L: And answering them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says, "O unbelieving generation, how long will I be with you?
en.B: Jesus answered them, "You unbelieving generation! How long must I stay with you?
en.R: Jesus said to them, "You people do not believe! How long do I have to stay with you?

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đáp lời họ và nói: "Hỡi thế hệ không tin, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ ở với các người cho đến bao giờ?
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Ôi, thế hệ vô tín! Ta phải ở với các người cho đến bao giờ?
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Các người thật không có lòng tin! Ta còn phải ở với các người bao lâu nữa?

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 그들에게 대답하여 말씀하신다. "오, 믿음이 없는 세대여, 내가 언제까지 너희와 함께 있겠느냐?
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 대답하셨다. "믿음이 없는 세대여! 내가 언제까지 너희와 함께 있어야 하겠느냐?
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "너희는 어찌 이렇게 믿지 않느냐! 내가 언제까지 너희와 함께 있어야 하겠느냐?

es.L: Y respondiéndoles, dice: «¡Oh generación incrédula! ¿Hasta cuándo estaré con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?
es.B: Jesús les respondió: «¡Generación incrédula! ¿Hasta cuándo tendré que estar con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «¡Ay, gente sin fe! ¿Hasta cuándo tendré que quedarme con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?

fr.L: Et leur répondant, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Ô génération incrédule, jusqu’à quand serai-je avec vous ?
fr.B: Jésus leur répondit : « Génération incrédule ! Jusqu’à quand devrai-je rester avec vous ?
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit : « Vous ne croyez donc pas ! Combien de temps faudra-t-il encore que je reste avec vous ?

sw.L: Naye akiwajibu, anasema, "Ewe kizazi kisichoamini, nitakuwa pamoja nanyi mpaka lini?
sw.B: Yesu akawajibu, "Ninyi kizazi kisichoamini! Nitakaa nanyi mpaka lini?
sw.R: Yesu akawaambia, "Ninyi watu hamuamini! Nitaendelea kukaa nanyi mpaka lini?

pt.L: E ele, respondendo-lhes, diz: "Ó geração incrédula, até quando estarei com vocês?
pt.B: Jesus lhes respondeu: "Geração sem fé! Até quando terei de ficar com vocês?
pt.R: Jesus disse a eles: "Vocês não têm fé! Até quando vou ter de ficar com vocês?

decisions.choice: them: the whole company, disciples, father, crowd and scribes
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to all of them. The word "generation" takes in the people of his time, the disciples included, since they failed (9:18).

decisions.choice: unbelieving generation: Israel's lack of faith in the wilderness
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 32:5 and 32:20 speak of a crooked generation, children without faithfulness. As Moses came down Sinai to find unfaithfulness (Exodus 32), Jesus comes down to find unbelief.

decisions.choice: unbelieving: without trust in God
decisions.reason: The word is the opposite of believing. It points ahead to the father's words in 9:24.

decisions.choice: says: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Another of Mark's vivid presents. The sense is past.

decisions.choice: You people do not believe!
decisions.reason: Readable turns the address into a plain statement.

decisions.choice: "các người" for "you"
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the whole company, disciples, father, crowd and scribes, so he uses the word for a crowd.

decisions.choice: "믿음이 없는 세대" (L, B); "믿지 않느냐" (R)
decisions.reason: "Unbelieving" is lack of trust in God (meaning decision); Korean keeps the link with "믿다" and "믿음" in 9:23-24 at every level. Readable turns the address into a plain exclamation, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: ¡Ay, gente sin fe!
decisions.reason: Readable says what an "unbelieving generation" is in everyday words, as the English "You people do not believe!" does.

decisions.choice: geração incrédula (L); Geração sem fé (B)
decisions.reason: The same words as Matthew 17:17. Balanced says "sem fé" so that the rebuke links with the father's "Eu creio" in 9:24 (m3).

source.text: ἕως πότε ἀνέξομαι ὑμῶν;

records.literal_gloss: Until when will I bear with you?

en.L: How long will I put up with you?
en.B: How long must I bear with you?
en.R: How long must I be patient with you?

vi.L: Ta sẽ chịu đựng các người cho đến bao giờ?
vi.B: Ta phải chịu đựng các người cho đến bao giờ?
vi.R: Ta còn phải kiên nhẫn với các người bao lâu nữa?

sw.B: Basi wakamleta mtoto {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}.
sw.R: Basi wakamleta mtoto kwa Yesu.

pt.R: Então trouxeram o menino até Jesus.

records.literal_gloss: And having seen him, the spirit immediately threw into convulsions him, and having fallen on the ground he was rolling around, foaming.

en.L: And when the spirit saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, it immediately threw him into convulsions, and falling on the ground, he rolled around, foaming.
en.B: As soon as the spirit saw Jesus, it threw the boy into a fit. He fell to the ground and rolled about, foaming at the mouth.
en.R: When the evil spirit saw Jesus, right away it made the boy shake violently. The boy fell on the ground. He rolled around, and foam came out of his mouth.

vi.L: Và vừa thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, linh ấy lập tức làm cho nó co giật, và nó ngã xuống đất, lăn lộn, sùi bọt.
vi.B: Vừa thấy Đức Giê-xu, linh ấy lập tức làm cho đứa bé lên cơn co giật. Nó ngã xuống đất, lăn lộn và sùi bọt mép.
vi.R: Khi thấy Đức Giê-xu, tà linh ấy liền làm cho đứa bé co giật dữ dội. Đứa bé ngã xuống đất. Nó lăn lộn, miệng sùi bọt.

ko.L: 그리고 그 영이 그분을 보자, 곧 그를 경련을 일으키게 했다. 그리고 그는 땅에 넘어져 거품을 흘리며 뒹굴었다.
ko.B: 그 영이 예수를 보자 곧바로 아이에게 심한 경련을 일으켰다. 아이는 땅에 넘어져 입에 거품을 물고 뒹굴었다.
ko.R: 악한 영이 예수를 보자, 바로 아이의 몸을 심하게 흔들어 댔다. 아이는 땅바닥에 넘어졌다. 그리고 입에서 거품을 흘리며 이리저리 뒹굴었다.

es.L: Y al verlo, el espíritu enseguida lo sacudió con convulsiones, y cayendo en tierra, se revolcaba echando espuma.
es.B: En cuanto el espíritu vio a Jesús, sacudió al muchacho con un ataque. El muchacho cayó al suelo y se revolcaba echando espuma por la boca.
es.R: Cuando el espíritu maligno vio a Jesús, enseguida hizo que el muchacho temblara con violencia. El muchacho cayó al suelo. Se revolcaba, y le salía espuma por la boca.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} voyant, l’esprit aussitôt le secoua de convulsions, et tombant à terre, il se roulait en écumant.
fr.B: Dès que l’esprit vit Jésus, il secoua l’enfant de convulsions. L’enfant tomba à terre et se roulait en écumant.
fr.R: Quand l’esprit mauvais a vu Jésus, il a tout de suite fait trembler le garçon très fort. Le garçon est tombé par terre. Il se roulait sur le sol, et de l’écume sortait de sa bouche.

sw.L: Na pepo alipomwona, mara moja akamtetemesha kwa nguvu, naye akianguka chini akagaagaa, akitoa povu.
sw.B: Pepo yule alipomwona Yesu, mara moja alimtetemesha mtoto kwa nguvu. Mtoto akaanguka chini, akagaagaa huku akitokwa na povu kinywani.
sw.R: Pepo mbaya alipomwona Yesu, mara moja alimfanya mtoto atetemeke kwa nguvu. Mtoto akaanguka chini. Akagaagaa, na povu likamtoka kinywani.

pt.L: E, ao vê-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}, o espírito imediatamente o agitou com convulsões, e, caindo no chão, ele rolava, espumando.
pt.B: Assim que viu Jesus, o espírito sacudiu o menino numa convulsão. Ele caiu no chão e rolava de um lado para o outro, espumando pela boca.
pt.R: Quando o espírito mau viu Jesus, na mesma hora fez o menino tremer com força. O menino caiu no chão. Ele rolava, e saía espuma da boca dele.

decisions.choice: having seen him: the spirit saw Jesus
decisions.reason: The participle is masculine though "spirit" is neuter. It is joined to the spirit by sense, as a person. It could be read of the boy, but the spirit is the subject of the main verb.

decisions.choice: threw into convulsions: shook him violently
decisions.reason: The verb means to tear or shake about. It describes the seizure.

decisions.choice: was rolling around: went on rolling about
decisions.reason: The imperfect describes continuing movement.

decisions.choice: Jesus; the boy
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who is meant by each pronoun.

decisions.choice: akamtetemesha kwa nguvu (shook him violently)
decisions.reason: "Kifafa" is the name of epilepsy and "degedege" of fits in small children; either would name an illness. The verb says what the spirit did, as the meaning decision describes it: it shook him violently.

en.B: Jesus asked the boy's father, "Since when has this been happening to him?"
en.R: Jesus asked the boy's father, "When did this start happening to your son?"

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hỏi cha nó: "Việc này xảy đến với nó đã bao lâu rồi?"

vi.R: Đức Giê-xu hỏi cha đứa bé: "Con ông bắt đầu bị như vậy từ khi nào?"

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 그의 아버지에게 물으셨다. "이런 일이 그에게 일어난 지 얼마나 되었느냐?"

ko.R: 예수께서 아이의 아버지에게 물으셨다. "네 아들에게 이런 일이 언제부터 생겼느냐?"

es.R: Jesús le preguntó al padre del muchacho: «¿Cuándo empezó a pasarle esto a tu hijo?».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} demanda à son père : « Combien de temps y a-t-il que cela lui arrive ? »
fr.B: Jésus demanda au père de l’enfant : « Depuis quand cela lui arrive-t-il ? »
fr.R: Jésus a demandé au père du garçon : « Quand est-ce que cela a commencé pour ton fils ? »

sw.R: Yesu akamwuliza baba wa mtoto, "Hali hii ilianza kumpata mwanao lini?"

pt.R: Jesus perguntou ao pai do menino: "Quando isso começou a acontecer com o seu filho?"

decisions.choice: this: the attacks

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks to the father in 해라체
decisions.reason: As throughout (style guide, section 4): Jesus speaks to petitioners in the plain style, which in Korean marks his authority as teacher rather than rudeness.

decisions.choice: from childhood: since he was very young
decisions.reason: The word points to early childhood. The boy is still a child (9:24).

decisions.choice: The father
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

records.literal_gloss: and often both into fire him it cast and into waters, that it might destroy him; but if anything you are able, help us, having compassion on us.

en.L: and often it has thrown him both into fire and into water, to destroy him; but if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are able [to do] anything, help us, having compassion on us."
en.B: Many times it has thrown him into fire or into water to kill him. But if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are able to do anything at all, help us. Have pity on us!"
en.R: The spirit has often thrown him into fire or into water to try to kill him. If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can do anything, please feel sorry for us and help us!"

vi.L: và nhiều lần nó đã ném cháu cả vào lửa lẫn vào nước để giết cháu; nhưng nếu Thầy có thể [làm] được gì, xin động lòng thương xót chúng tôi mà giúp chúng tôi."
vi.B: Nhiều lần nó ném cháu vào lửa hoặc xuống nước để giết cháu. Nhưng nếu Thầy làm được điều gì, xin thương xót mà giúp chúng tôi!"
vi.R: Tà linh ấy đã nhiều lần ném cháu vào lửa hay xuống nước để tìm cách giết cháu. Nếu Thầy làm được gì, xin Thầy thương xót và giúp đỡ chúng tôi!"

ko.L: 그리고 [그 영이] 여러 번 그를 불 속에도 던지고 물속에도 [던졌습니다]. 그를 죽이려고 한 것입니다. 그러나 선생님께서 무엇이든 하실 수 있으면, 저희를 불쌍히 여기셔서 저희를 도와주십시오."
ko.B: 그 영이 아이를 죽이려고 여러 번 불 속에도 던지고 물속에도 던졌습니다. 하실 수 있는 일이 무엇이든 있으시면, 저희를 불쌍히 여기시고 도와주십시오!"
ko.R: 그 영은 아이를 죽이려고 여러 번 불 속에도 던지고 물속에도 던졌습니다. 선생님께서 무엇이라도 하실 수 있으면, 저희를 불쌍히 여기셔서 도와주십시오!"

es.L: y muchas veces lo ha arrojado tanto al fuego como al agua para destruirlo; pero si puedes [hacer] algo, ayúdanos, teniendo compasión de nosotros».
es.B: Muchas veces lo ha arrojado al fuego o al agua para matarlo. Pero si puedes hacer algo, ayúdanos. ¡Ten compasión de nosotros!».
es.R: El espíritu muchas veces lo ha tirado al fuego o al agua para intentar matarlo. Si puedes hacer algo, ¡por favor, ten compasión de nosotros y ayúdanos!».

fr.L: et souvent il l’a jeté et dans le feu et dans les eaux, pour le faire périr ; mais si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} peux [faire] quelque chose, viens-nous en aide, ayant pitié de nous. »
fr.B: Bien des fois, l’esprit l’a jeté dans le feu ou dans l’eau pour le faire mourir. Mais si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} peux faire quelque chose, viens à notre secours. Aie pitié de nous ! »
fr.R: Souvent, l’esprit l’a jeté dans le feu ou dans l’eau pour essayer de le tuer. Si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} peux faire quelque chose, aie pitié de nous et aide-nous ! »

sw.L: na mara nyingi amemtupa motoni na majini ili amwangamize; lakini ukiweza [kufanya] lolote, utusaidie, ukituhurumia."
sw.B: Mara nyingi amemtupa motoni au majini ili amwue. Lakini kama unaweza kufanya lolote, utuhurumie, utusaidie!"
sw.R: Pepo huyo amemtupa mara nyingi motoni au majini ili kujaribu kumwua. Ikiwa unaweza kufanya chochote, tafadhali utuhurumie, utusaidie!"

pt.L: e muitas vezes o lançou tanto no fogo como na água, para destruí-lo; mas, se {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} podes alguma coisa, ajuda-nos, tendo compaixão de nós."
pt.B: Muitas vezes o espírito o jogou no fogo ou na água para matá-lo. Mas, se {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} podes fazer alguma coisa, ajuda-nos. Tem compaixão de nós!"
pt.R: Muitas vezes o espírito jogou o menino no fogo ou na água para tentar matá-lo. Se {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} podes fazer alguma coisa, por favor, tem pena de nós e ajuda-nos!"

decisions.choice: has thrown: the spirit has done this again and again
decisions.reason: "Often" shows that the past tense sums up many attacks.

decisions.choice: if you are able: the father is not sure Jesus can help
decisions.reason: After the disciples failed, the father doubts. Jesus takes up these words in 9:23.

decisions.choice: having compassion: deep pity
decisions.reason: The verb speaks of feeling stirred within. Mark uses it of Jesus himself (1:41; 6:34; 8:2).

decisions.choice: us: the father counts himself with his son
decisions.reason: The father shares his son's suffering and asks for both of them.

decisions.choice: the spirit; to try to
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject and shows that the spirit's aim had not succeeded.

decisions.choice: [그 영이]; [던졌습니다]
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves the subject to the verb and uses one verb for both fire and water; Korean needs the subject and repeats the verb, so Literal brackets both.

decisions.choice: "저희" for "us"
decisions.reason: The father counts himself with his son (meaning decision) and speaks humbly to Jesus, so the humble "저희" fits every level, as people speaking to Jesus about themselves say it throughout the Korean Mark.

decisions.choice: se tu podes
decisions.reason: Portuguese usually drops the subject pronoun, but the father's "tu" is kept here because Jesus throws his words back at him in 9:23 (m2), and the two must match.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Τὸ Εἰ δύνῃ, πάντα δυνατὰ τῷ πιστεύοντι.

records.literal_gloss: And Jesus said to him, The If you are able! All things are possible to the [one] believing.

en.L: And Jesus said to him, "'If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are able!' All things [are] possible for the one who believes."
en.B: Jesus said to him, "'If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can!' All things are possible for the one who believes."
en.R: Jesus said to him, "Why do you say, 'If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can'? Everything is possible for a person who believes."

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu nói với ông: "'Nếu Thầy có thể!' Mọi sự đều có thể cho người tin."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nói với ông: "'Nếu Thầy có thể!' Mọi việc đều có thể được đối với người tin."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với ông: "Sao ông lại nói: 'Nếu Thầy có thể'? Mọi việc đều có thể làm được cho người có lòng tin."

ko.L: 그러자 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "'하실 수 있으면'이라니! 믿는 사람에게는 모든 것이 가능하다."
ko.B: 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "'하실 수 있으면'이라고 했느냐? 믿는 사람에게는 무엇이든 할 수 있다."
ko.R: 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "왜 '하실 수 있으면'이라고 말하느냐? 믿는 사람에게는 무엇이든지 다 가능하다."

es.L: Y Jesús le dijo: «¡“Si puedes”! Todo [es] posible para el que cree».
es.B: Jesús le dijo: «¡“Si puedes”! Todo es posible para el que cree».
es.R: Jesús le dijo: «¿Por qué dices “si puedes”? Todo es posible para la persona que cree».

fr.L: Et Jésus lui dit : « “Si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} peux !” Tout [est] possible à celui qui croit. »
fr.B: Jésus lui dit : « “Si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} peux !” Tout est possible pour celui qui croit. »
fr.R: Jésus lui a dit : « Pourquoi dis-tu : “Si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} peux” ? Tout est possible pour celui qui croit. »

sw.L: Naye Yesu akamwambia, "'Ukiweza!' Mambo yote [yanawezekana] kwa anayeamini."
sw.B: Yesu akamwambia, "'Kama unaweza!' Kila kitu kinawezekana kwa mtu anayeamini."
sw.R: Yesu akamwambia, "Kwa nini unasema, 'Kama unaweza'? Kila jambo linawezekana kwa mtu anayeamini."

pt.L: E Jesus lhe disse: "'Se {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} podes!' Tudo [é] possível para quem crê."
pt.B: Jesus lhe disse: "'Se {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} podes!' Tudo é possível para quem crê."
pt.R: Jesus disse ao pai: "Por que você diz: 'Se {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} podes'? Tudo é possível para a pessoa que acredita."

decisions.choice: 'If you are able!': Jesus repeats the father's words and throws them back
alternatives: Jesus asks if he himself is able
decisions.reason: The article points to the father's phrase as a quotation. The question is not whether Jesus is able but whether the father will trust.

decisions.choice: 'If you are able!', the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: If you are able to believe, all things are possible
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "to believe", which smooths the grammar and makes it a condition placed on the father. The shorter reading is found in the earliest manuscripts. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the one who believes: the father, who answers in 9:24
alternatives: Jesus himself, whose trust in God makes all things possible
decisions.reason: The father replies "I believe", so he takes the words to mean him. Some see Jesus' own trust in God in them too. The two are not exclusive.

decisions.choice: believes: trusts God and his power at work in Jesus
decisions.reason: Believing in Mark is trust that God will act (5:36; 11:22-24).

decisions.choice: Why do you say
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that Jesus is quoting the father.

decisions.choice: Jesus repeats the father's own words, "Nếu Thầy có thể", with the father's "Thầy" kept and no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Vietnamese changes the pronoun with the speaker; keeping the father's "Thầy" lets the reader hear that Jesus is quoting him and throwing the words back, as the meaning decision says.

decisions.choice: "người tin" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese words are already inclusive.

decisions.choice: "'하실 수 있으면'이라니" (L); "... 했느냐?" (B); "왜 ... 말하느냐?" (R)
decisions.reason: Jesus throws the father's words back at him (meaning decision); Korean quotes them with the honorific the father used, and each level marks the quotation as Jesus's retort in its own way.

decisions.choice: “Si puedes” in inner quotation marks
decisions.reason: Jesus throws the father's own words back at him (meaning decision); the Spanish quotes them inside his reply, with the inner marks the Spanish uses within «».

decisions.choice: 'Se tu podes!', quoted with the father's "tu"
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes the father's own words, so they keep the father's address to him, "tu"; Jesus himself speaks to the father with "você" (R: "Por que você diz"), as he does to any person (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4).

source.text: εὐθὺς κράξας ὁ πατὴρ τοῦ παιδίου ἔλεγεν· Πιστεύω· βοήθει μου τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: Immediately having cried out the father of the child was saying, I believe; help of me the unbelief.

en.L: Immediately the father of the child cried out and said, "I believe; help my unbelief!"
en.B: At once the boy's father cried out, "I believe! Help my unbelief!"
en.R: Right away the boy's father shouted, "I do believe! Help me with my unbelief!"

vi.L: Lập tức cha của đứa trẻ kêu lớn và nói: "Tôi tin; xin giúp sự vô tín của tôi!"
vi.B: Ngay lúc ấy cha đứa bé kêu lên: "Tôi tin! Xin giúp tôi khỏi sự vô tín!"
vi.R: Ngay lập tức người cha kêu lớn: "Tôi tin chứ! Xin Thầy giúp tôi ở những chỗ tôi còn thiếu lòng tin!"

ko.L: 곧 그 아이의 아버지가 소리쳐 말했다. "제가 믿습니다. 믿음이 없는 저를 도와주십시오."
ko.B: 곧바로 아이의 아버지가 소리쳤다. "믿습니다! 제 믿음 없는 것을 도와주십시오!"
ko.R: 바로 그때 아이의 아버지가 크게 외쳤다. "저는 믿습니다! 제 믿음이 부족한 것을 도와주십시오!"

es.L: Enseguida el padre del niño gritó y decía: «¡Creo! ¡Ayuda a mi incredulidad!».
es.B: Al instante el padre del muchacho gritó: «¡Creo! ¡Ayúdame en mi incredulidad!».
es.R: Enseguida el padre del muchacho gritó: «¡Sí, creo! ¡Ayúdame cuando me falta la fe!».

fr.L: Aussitôt le père de l’enfant s’écria et dit : « Je crois ; viens en aide à mon incrédulité ! »
fr.B: Aussitôt le père de l’enfant s’écria : « Je crois ! Viens au secours de mon incrédulité ! »
fr.R: Tout de suite, le père du garçon a crié : « Oui, je crois ! Aide-moi là où ma foi est trop faible ! »

sw.L: Mara moja baba wa mtoto akapaza sauti, akasema, "Ninaamini; saidia kutoamini kwangu!"
sw.B: Mara moja baba wa mtoto akapaza sauti, "Ninaamini! Nisaidie pale imani yangu inapopungua!"
sw.R: Mara moja baba wa mtoto akapiga kelele, "Ninaamini kweli! Nisaidie nishinde kutoamini kwangu!"

pt.L: Imediatamente o pai do menino, clamando, dizia: "Creio; ajuda a minha incredulidade!"
pt.B: Na mesma hora, o pai do menino gritou: "Eu creio! Socorre a minha falta de fé!"
pt.R: Logo o pai do menino gritou: "Eu creio, sim! Ajuda-me com a minha falta de fé!"

decisions.choice: cried out, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "with tears" and address Jesus as "Lord". The earliest manuscripts lack both. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: help my unbelief: help me where my faith falls short
decisions.reason: The father admits that his trust is mixed with doubt and asks Jesus to help him in that weakness.

decisions.choice: believe, unbelief: the same word family as 9:19 and 9:23
decisions.reason: Believing and unbelief are set side by side in one man.

decisions.choice: Help me with my unbelief
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the father asks help for himself.

decisions.choice: "giúp tôi khỏi sự vô tín" (B); "giúp tôi ở những chỗ tôi còn thiếu lòng tin" (R)
alternatives: "giúp đỡ sự vô tín của tôi"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese cannot "help" an unbelief as an object without sounding odd; Balanced and Readable say what the meaning decision says he asks: help where his faith falls short.

decisions.choice: "믿음이 없는 저" (L); "제 믿음 없는 것" (B); "제 믿음이 부족한 것" (R)
decisions.reason: "Help my unbelief" means help me where my faith falls short (meaning decision); "불신" in Korean sounds like distrust of a person. Every level keeps "믿음", linked with "믿다" in 9:19 and 9:23.

decisions.choice: ¡Ayúdame cuando me falta la fe!
decisions.reason: "Incredulidad" is a hard word for new readers; Readable says what it means, help me where my faith falls short (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: incrédulité (L, B)
decisions.reason: "Incrédulité" keeps the link with "incrédule" in 9:19, the same word family in Greek (meaning decision on believe and unbelief); Readable says what it means, as the meaning decision does.

decisions.choice: Nisaidie pale imani yangu inapopungua (B); Nisaidie nishinde kutoamini kwangu (R)
alternatives: saidia kutoamini kwangu at every level
decisions.reason: "Kutoamini" keeps the word family of believing (9:19, 9:23) at Literal. Balanced says what the meaning decision describes, help where my faith falls short; Readable keeps the word and adds "nishinde" (help me overcome), as the English Readable says "help me with my unbelief".

decisions.choice: Socorre a minha falta de fé (B); Ajuda-me com a minha falta de fé (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "incredulidade", the word of the same family as "crer" (m3). Balanced and Readable say "falta de fé", the everyday phrase; Balanced uses "socorrer", which takes a thing in need as its object more easily than "ajudar", and Readable says plainly that the father asks help for himself, as the English Readable does.

source.text: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἐπισυντρέχει ὄχλος ἐπετίμησεν τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἀκαθάρτῳ λέγων αὐτῷ· Τὸ ἄλαλον καὶ κωφὸν πνεῦμα, ἐγὼ ἐπιτάσσω σοι, ἔξελθε ἐξ αὐτοῦ καὶ μηκέτι εἰσέλθῃς εἰς αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Having seen now Jesus that was running together a crowd, he rebuked the spirit, the unclean, saying to it, Mute and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him and no more may you enter into him.

en.L: Now when Jesus saw that a crowd was running together, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it, "Mute and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him and never enter him again."
en.B: When Jesus saw that a crowd was quickly gathering, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave the unclean spirit a stern order: "You mute and deaf spirit, I command you to come out of him and never go into him again!"
en.R: Jesus saw that more people were running over to see. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke sternly to the evil spirit. "You spirit that makes this boy deaf and unable to speak," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I order you to come out of him! Never go back into him again!"

vi.L: Bấy giờ Đức Giê-xu thấy đám đông đang kéo nhau chạy đến, thì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} quở trách linh ô uế, nói với nó: "Hỡi linh câm và điếc, chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} truyền lệnh cho ngươi: hãy ra khỏi nó, và đừng bao giờ nhập vào nó nữa!"
vi.B: Khi Đức Giê-xu thấy dân chúng đang kéo đến đông thêm, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nghiêm khắc ra lệnh cho linh ô uế: "Hỡi linh câm và điếc kia, chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} truyền lệnh cho ngươi phải ra khỏi đứa bé này và đừng bao giờ nhập vào nó nữa!"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu thấy người ta đang chạy đến xem ngày càng đông. Vì vậy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nghiêm khắc ra lệnh cho tà linh: "Hỡi tà linh làm cho đứa bé này câm và điếc, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ra lệnh cho ngươi phải ra khỏi nó! Đừng bao giờ nhập vào nó nữa!"

ko.L: 예수께서는 무리가 달려와 모여드는 것을 보시고, 더러운 영을 꾸짖으며 그에게 말씀하셨다. "말 못 하고 듣지 못하게 하는 영아, 내가 네게 명령한다. 그에게서 나오너라. 그리고 다시는 그에게 들어가지 마라."
ko.B: 예수께서는 무리가 몰려드는 것을 보시고, 더러운 영을 엄하게 꾸짖으셨다. "말 못 하고 듣지 못하게 하는 영아, 내가 네게 명령한다. 이 아이에게서 나오너라. 다시는 이 아이에게 들어가지 마라!"
ko.R: 예수께서는 사람들이 더 많이 달려오는 것을 보셨다. 그래서 악한 영에게 엄하게 말씀하셨다. "이 아이를 듣지도 말하지도 못하게 하는 영아, 내가 너에게 명령한다. 이 아이에게서 나와라! 다시는 이 아이 속에 들어가지 마라!"

es.L: Y viendo Jesús que una multitud se agolpaba corriendo, reprendió al espíritu impuro, diciéndole: «Espíritu mudo y sordo, yo te ordeno: sal de él y no vuelvas a entrar en él».
es.B: Cuando Jesús vio que la multitud se juntaba rápidamente, reprendió al espíritu impuro: «Espíritu mudo y sordo, yo te ordeno que salgas de él y que nunca vuelvas a entrar en él».
es.R: Jesús vio que más gente venía corriendo a ver. Así que le habló con firmeza al espíritu maligno. Le dijo: «Espíritu que no dejas hablar ni oír a este muchacho, ¡yo te ordeno que salgas de él! ¡Nunca vuelvas a entrar en él!».

fr.L: Or Jésus, voyant qu’une foule accourait, réprimanda l’esprit impur, lui disant : « Esprit muet et sourd, {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je te l’ordonne : sors de lui et n’entre plus jamais en lui. »
fr.B: Quand Jésus vit que la foule accourait en nombre, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} donna un ordre sévère à l’esprit impur : « Esprit muet et sourd, je te l’ordonne : sors de cet enfant et n’y rentre plus jamais ! »
fr.R: Jésus a vu que d’autres gens arrivaient en courant. Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a parlé sévèrement à l’esprit mauvais. « Toi, l’esprit qui rend ce garçon sourd et muet, a-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit, je t’ordonne de sortir de lui ! Ne rentre plus jamais en lui ! »

sw.L: Lakini Yesu alipoona kwamba umati unakusanyika mbio, akamkemea yule pepo mchafu, akimwambia, "Wewe pepo bubu na kiziwi, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nakuamuru, toka ndani yake, wala usimwingie tena kamwe."
sw.B: Yesu alipoona kwamba umati ulikuwa ukikusanyika kwa haraka, alimkemea yule pepo mchafu, akisema, "Wewe pepo bubu na kiziwi, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nakuamuru: toka ndani yake, wala usimwingie tena kamwe!"
sw.R: Yesu aliona kwamba watu wengi zaidi walikuwa wakija mbio kuona. Basi akamkemea yule pepo mbaya, akasema, "Wewe pepo unayemfanya kijana huyu kuwa kiziwi na asiweze kusema, nakuamuru umtoke! Usimwingie tena kamwe!"

pt.L: Mas Jesus, vendo que uma multidão vinha correndo para se ajuntar, repreendeu o espírito impuro, dizendo-lhe: "Espírito mudo e surdo, eu lhe ordeno: saia dele e nunca mais entre nele."
pt.B: Quando Jesus viu que mais gente vinha correndo e a multidão crescia, deu uma ordem severa ao espírito impuro: "Espírito mudo e surdo, eu lhe ordeno que saia dele e nunca mais entre nele!"
pt.R: Jesus viu que mais pessoas estavam vindo correndo para ver. Então {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} falou duramente com o espírito mau. "Espírito que deixa este menino surdo e sem fala", disse {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}, "eu ordeno que você saia dele! Nunca mais entre nele!"

decisions.choice: a crowd was running together: more people were gathering
decisions.reason: The word suggests people running up to join. Jesus acts before a larger crowd forms.

decisions.choice: rebuked: commanded sternly
decisions.reason: The same verb Jesus uses with spirits and with the storm (1:25; 4:39).

decisions.choice: I: emphatic, I myself command you
decisions.reason: Jesus stresses his own authority, where the disciples had failed.

decisions.choice: never enter him again: the cure is permanent
decisions.reason: The command shuts the spirit out for good, since its attacks had come and gone (9:18).

decisions.choice: You spirit that makes this boy deaf and unable to speak
decisions.reason: Readable says what the spirit's name means.

decisions.choice: "linh ô uế" (L, B); "tà linh" (R) for the unclean spirit
decisions.reason: "ô uế" keeps the Greek "unclean" in plain modern Vietnamese; Readable uses the common word for an evil spirit.

decisions.choice: "ngươi" for "you" when Jesus commands the spirit; "chính Ta" (L, B) for the emphatic "I"
decisions.reason: "ngươi" is the word for a commanding speaker addressing an inferior or hostile being, without the vulgarity of "mày".

decisions.choice: "더러운 영" (L, B); "악한 영" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 3: "더러운 영" keeps Mark's word "unclean"; Readable says "악한 영" as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks to the spirit in 해라체 with the emphatic "내가"
decisions.reason: "I" is emphatic (meaning decision); the subject particle "가" carries the stress in Korean.

decisions.choice: espíritu impuro (L, B); espíritu maligno (R)
decisions.reason: "Unclean" means unfit for God's presence; "impuro" says that. Readable says plainly that the spirit is evil, as the English does.

decisions.choice: l’esprit impur (L, B); l’esprit mauvais (R)
decisions.reason: "Impur" keeps the sense of ritual uncleanness that the Greek has; "immonde" is older church French. Readable says plainly "esprit mauvais", as the English Readable says "evil spirit".

decisions.choice: moi, je te l’ordonne (L)
decisions.reason: The emphatic "I" (meaning decision) is shown in French Literal by a stressed "moi".

decisions.choice: pepo mchafu (unclean spirit) at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: "Mchafu" (unclean) is the plain word; "najisi" is ritual uncleanness and would narrow the sense. "Pepo mchafu" as in 1:23; plain "pepo" in 9:38 names the same kind of being.

decisions.choice: eu lhe ordeno ... saia (L, B); eu ordeno que você saia (R)
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the spirit as to anyone else, with the "você" forms ("lhe", "saia"); "tu" is kept for speaking to God and to Jesus (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4). Readable avoids "lhe" with an explicit "você"; Matthew does the same with Satan (4:10).

source.text: καὶ κράξας καὶ πολλὰ σπαράξας ἐξῆλθεν· καὶ ἐγένετο ὡσεὶ νεκρὸς ὥστε τοὺς πολλοὺς λέγειν ὅτι ἀπέθανεν.

records.literal_gloss: And having cried out and much having convulsed [him], it came out; and he became as if dead, so that the many said that he died.

en.L: And after crying out and convulsing [him] greatly, it came out; and he became like [one] dead, so that the many said, "He has died."
en.B: The spirit shrieked, threw him into violent convulsions, and came out. The boy was left lying like a corpse, so that most of them said, "He has died."
en.R: The spirit screamed and shook the boy hard. Then it came out of him. The boy looked as if he were dead, and many people said, "He is dead."

vi.L: Và sau khi kêu thét và làm cho [nó] co giật dữ dội, [linh ấy] ra khỏi; và nó trở nên như [người] chết, đến nỗi phần đông nói rằng: "Nó chết rồi."
vi.B: Linh ấy rú lên, làm cho đứa bé co giật dữ dội, rồi ra khỏi. Đứa bé nằm như xác chết, đến nỗi phần đông đều nói: "Nó chết rồi."
vi.R: Tà linh hét lên và làm cho đứa bé co giật mạnh. Rồi nó ra khỏi đứa bé. Đứa bé nằm im như đã chết, và nhiều người nói: "Nó chết rồi!"

ko.L: 그러자 [그 영이] 소리를 지르고 그를 심하게 경련을 일으키게 한 뒤 나갔다. 그리고 그는 죽은 [사람]처럼 되었으므로, 많은 사람이 "그가 죽었다" 하고 말했다.
ko.B: 그 영은 소리를 지르며 아이에게 심한 경련을 일으키고는 나갔다. 아이는 죽은 사람처럼 되어 버려서, 대부분의 사람이 "아이가 죽었다" 하고 말했다.
ko.R: 악한 영은 소리를 지르고 아이를 세게 흔들어 놓고 나서 아이에게서 나갔다. 아이는 죽은 것처럼 보였다. 그래서 많은 사람이 "아이가 죽었다" 하고 말했다.

es.L: Y después de gritar y sacudir[lo] violentamente, salió; y quedó como muerto, de modo que la mayoría decía: «Ha muerto».
es.B: El espíritu dio un alarido, lo sacudió con violentas convulsiones y salió. El muchacho quedó tendido como un cadáver, de modo que la mayoría decía: «Ha muerto».
es.R: El espíritu gritó y sacudió al muchacho con fuerza. Luego salió de él. El muchacho parecía muerto, y muchos decían: «Está muerto».

fr.L: Et ayant crié et [l’]ayant violemment secoué, il sortit ; et il devint comme mort, si bien que la plupart disaient : « Il est mort. »
fr.B: L’esprit poussa un cri, secoua l’enfant de violentes convulsions et sortit. L’enfant resta étendu comme un cadavre, si bien que la plupart disaient : « Il est mort. »
fr.R: L’esprit a crié et a secoué le garçon très fort. Puis il est sorti de lui. Le garçon avait l’air mort, et beaucoup de gens disaient : « Il est mort. »

sw.L: Na baada ya kupiga kelele na kumtikisa sana, akatoka; naye akawa kama mfu, hata wengi wakasema kwamba amekufa.
sw.B: Pepo huyo akapiga ukelele, akamtikisa kwa nguvu sana, kisha akatoka. Mtoto akabaki amelala kama maiti, hata wengi wakasema, "Amekufa."
sw.R: Pepo akapiga kelele na kumtikisa mtoto kwa nguvu. Kisha akamtoka. Mtoto alionekana kama aliyekufa, na watu wengi wakasema, "Amekufa."

pt.L: E, depois de gritar e de agitá-[lo] muito, saiu; e ele ficou como [um] morto, de modo que muitos diziam: "Ele morreu."
pt.B: O espírito deu um grito, sacudiu o menino com violentas convulsões e saiu. O menino ficou estendido como um cadáver, de modo que a maioria dizia: "Ele morreu."
pt.R: O espírito gritou e sacudiu o menino com força. Depois saiu dele. O menino parecia morto, e muita gente disse: "Ele está morto."

decisions.choice: having cried out, having convulsed: the spirit is the subject
decisions.reason: The participles are masculine, as in 9:20, but they go with the spirit that comes out.

decisions.choice: the many: most of those there
decisions.reason: With the article the phrase means the majority.

decisions.choice: crying out: a shriek without words
decisions.reason: The spirit had made the boy mute, and no words are reported.

decisions.choice: like a corpse
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a vivid phrase for the boy's lifeless look.

decisions.choice: [그 영이]; [사람]
decisions.reason: The spirit is the subject of the participles (meaning decision) and Korean must name it; "죽은" needs a noun to stand on. Literal brackets both.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς κρατήσας τῆς χειρὸς αὐτοῦ ἤγειρεν αὐτόν, καὶ ἀνέστη.

records.literal_gloss: But Jesus having taken the hand of him raised him, and he arose.

en.L: But Jesus took him by the hand and raised him, and he arose.
en.B: But Jesus took hold of his hand and lifted him up, and he got to his feet.
en.R: But Jesus took the boy by the hand and helped him up. And the boy stood up.

vi.L: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu nắm lấy tay nó, nâng nó dậy, và nó đứng lên.
vi.B: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu cầm tay đứa bé, đỡ nó dậy, và nó đứng lên được.
vi.R: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu nắm tay đứa bé và giúp nó đứng dậy. Đứa bé đứng lên.

ko.L: 그러나 예수께서 그의 손을 잡아 그를 일으키시니, 그가 일어났다.
ko.B: 그러나 예수께서 아이의 손을 잡아 일으켜 주시자, 아이가 일어섰다.
ko.R: 그러나 예수께서 아이의 손을 잡고 일으켜 주셨다. 그러자 아이가 일어섰다.

es.L: Pero Jesús, tomándolo de la mano, lo levantó, y él se levantó.
es.B: Pero Jesús lo tomó de la mano y lo levantó, y él se puso de pie.
es.R: Pero Jesús tomó al muchacho de la mano y lo ayudó a levantarse. Y el muchacho se puso de pie.

fr.L: Mais Jésus, l’ayant pris par la main, le releva, et il se leva.
fr.B: Mais Jésus le prit par la main et le releva, et l’enfant se mit debout.
fr.R: Mais Jésus a pris le garçon par la main et l’a aidé à se relever. Et le garçon s’est mis debout.

sw.L: Lakini Yesu akamshika mkono, akamwinua, naye akainuka.
sw.B: Lakini Yesu akamshika mkono, akamwinua, naye akasimama.
sw.R: Lakini Yesu alimshika mtoto mkono, akamsaidia kuinuka. Na mtoto akasimama.

pt.L: Mas Jesus, tomando-o pela mão, o levantou, e ele se ergueu.
pt.B: Mas Jesus pegou a mão dele e o levantou, e ele ficou de pé.
pt.R: Mas Jesus pegou o menino pela mão e o ajudou a se levantar. E o menino ficou de pé.

decisions.choice: raised, arose: the verbs used for resurrection
decisions.reason: The same verbs describe rising from the dead (5:41-42; 9:9-10). The boy seemed dead, and Jesus raises him.

decisions.choice: but: in contrast to those who said he was dead
decisions.reason: The small word sets Jesus' act against the crowd's verdict.

decisions.choice: lifted him up, got to his feet (B); helped him up, stood up (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use everyday words. Literal keeps the words that recall resurrection.

decisions.choice: "일으키다" ... "일어나다/일어서다"
decisions.reason: The verbs are those used for resurrection (meaning decision); "일으키다" and "일어나다" are also the Korean words for raising the dead (9:9-10 "살아나다"), so the echo can still be heard without overstating it.

decisions.choice: lo levantó, y él se levantó
decisions.reason: Spanish "levantar(se)" is also said of rising from the dead, so Literal keeps the echo the meaning decision points to.

decisions.choice: akamwinua, naye akainuka
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the pair raise / arise in one Swahili root (kuinua, kuinuka), so the echo of resurrection that the meaning decision notes stays visible.

decisions.choice: o levantou ... se ergueu
decisions.reason: Portuguese has no pair of everyday verbs that are also the words for resurrection, as the Greek does (m1); "ressuscitar" would say he had died. Literal uses "levantar" and "erguer-se", which still recall rising.

source.text: καὶ εἰσελθόντος αὐτοῦ εἰς οἶκον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ κατ’ ἰδίαν ἐπηρώτων αὐτόν· Ὅτι ἡμεῖς οὐκ ἠδυνήθημεν ἐκβαλεῖν αὐτό;

records.literal_gloss: And having entered he into a house, the disciples of him in private were asking him, Why we not were able to cast out it?

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had gone into a house, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples were asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} privately, "Why were we not able to cast it out?"
en.B: After {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went indoors, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} privately, "Why could we not throw it out?"
en.R: Later Jesus went into a house. When {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers were alone with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they asked, "Why could we not force the spirit out?"

vi.L: Và khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã vào nhà, các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hỏi riêng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Sao chính chúng con lại không thể đuổi nó ra được?"
vi.B: Khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào nhà rồi, các môn đồ hỏi riêng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Sao chúng con không đuổi được nó?"
vi.R: Sau đó Đức Giê-xu vào một ngôi nhà. Khi các môn đồ ở riêng với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, họ hỏi: "Tại sao chúng con không đuổi được tà linh ấy ra?"

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 집에 들어가셨을 때, 그분의 제자들이 따로 그분께 물었다. "어찌하여 저희는 그것을 쫓아낼 수 없었습니까?"
ko.B: 예수께서 집에 들어가시자, 제자들이 따로 예수께 물었다. "왜 저희는 그 영을 쫓아내지 못했습니까?"
ko.R: 그 뒤에 예수께서 어떤 집에 들어가셨다. 제자들만 예수와 함께 있게 되자, 그들이 물었다. "왜 저희는 그 영을 쫓아내지 못했습니까?"

es.L: Y cuando entró en una casa, {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaban en privado: «¿Por qué nosotros no pudimos expulsarlo?».
es.B: Después de que entró en una casa, {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron a solas: «¿Por qué no pudimos expulsarlo nosotros?».
es.R: Más tarde, Jesús entró en una casa. Cuando {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos estuvieron a solas con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron: «¿Por qué no pudimos nosotros hacer salir al espíritu?».

fr.L: Et quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fut entré dans une maison, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}interrogeaient en privé : « Pourquoi nous, n’avons-nous pas pu le chasser ? »
fr.B: Une fois qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fut à l’intérieur, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demandèrent en privé : « Pourquoi n’avons-nous pas pu le chasser, nous ? »
fr.R: Plus tard, Jésus est entré dans une maison. Quand {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples ont été seuls avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont demandé : « Pourquoi est-ce que nous n’avons pas pu faire sortir l’esprit ? »

sw.L: Na alipokwisha kuingia nyumbani, wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walimwuliza faraghani, "Mbona sisi hatukuweza kumtoa?"
sw.B: Yesu alipoingia nyumbani, wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walimwuliza faraghani, "Kwa nini sisi hatukuweza kumfukuza?"
sw.R: Baadaye Yesu aliingia katika nyumba moja. Wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walipokuwa peke yao pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}, walimwuliza, "Kwa nini sisi hatukuweza kumtoa pepo yule?"

pt.L: E, quando {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} entrou em casa, os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} perguntavam em particular: "Por que nós não conseguimos expulsá-lo?"
pt.B: Depois que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} entrou em casa, os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} perguntaram em particular: "Por que nós não conseguimos expulsar aquele espírito?"
pt.R: Mais tarde, Jesus entrou numa casa. Quando os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} seguidores ficaram a sós com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}, perguntaram: "Por que nós não conseguimos fazer o espírito sair?"

decisions.choice: why: the small word opens a question
alternatives: that: we could not cast it out
decisions.reason: As in 9:11, the word introduces a question here.

decisions.choice: we: emphatic, we ourselves
decisions.reason: They had driven out demons before (6:13) and are puzzled that they failed.

decisions.choice: a house: a place for private teaching
decisions.reason: Mark often has Jesus explain things to the disciples alone in a house (7:17; 10:10).

decisions.choice: throw out (B); force out (R)
decisions.reason: The same pattern as in earlier chapters.

decisions.choice: "chúng con" for the disciples speaking to Jesus; "chính chúng con" (L) for the emphatic "we"
decisions.reason: The disciples call themselves "chúng con" before their teacher, as in John.

decisions.choice: "저희"
decisions.reason: The disciples speak humbly to their teacher in 합쇼체 and call themselves "저희" at every level, as throughout the Korean Mark; the emphatic "we" (meaning decision) is carried by the placement of "저희는".

decisions.choice: wanafunzi at every level
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "followers"; the Swahili says "wanafunzi" at every level, as Swahili John does, because the word is plain and familiar. For the whole chapter.

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τοῦτο τὸ γένος ἐν οὐδενὶ δύναται ἐξελθεῖν εἰ μὴ ἐν προσευχῇ.

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, This kind by nothing is able to go out except by prayer.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "This kind is not able to come out by anything except by prayer."
en.B: He told them, "This kind cannot be made to come out by any means except prayer."
en.R: Jesus answered, "Only prayer can make this kind of spirit come out."

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Loại này không thể ra bằng bất cứ cách nào, ngoại trừ bằng sự cầu nguyện."
vi.B: Ngài bảo họ: "Loại này không thể bị đuổi ra bằng cách nào khác ngoài sự cầu nguyện."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Chỉ có sự cầu nguyện mới đuổi được loại tà linh này ra thôi."

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "이런 종류는 기도가 아니고서는 무엇으로도 나갈 수 없다."
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "이런 종류는 기도 말고는 어떤 방법으로도 나가게 할 수 없다."
ko.R: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "이런 영은 기도로만 나가게 할 수 있다."

es.L: Y les dijo: «Esta clase con nada puede salir, sino con oración».
es.B: Les respondió: «Esta clase no puede salir por ningún medio, sino con oración».
es.R: Jesús respondió: «Solo la oración puede hacer que salga esta clase de espíritu».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Cette espèce-là ne peut sortir par rien, sinon par la prière. »
fr.B: Il leur répondit : « Cette espèce-là ne peut sortir par aucun moyen, sauf par la prière. »
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « Seule la prière peut faire sortir ce genre d’esprit. »

sw.L: Naye akawaambia, "Aina hii haiwezi kutoka kwa kitu chochote isipokuwa kwa maombi."
sw.B: Akawaambia, "Aina hii haiwezi kutolewa kwa njia yoyote ila kwa maombi."
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Ni maombi tu yanayoweza kumtoa pepo wa aina hii."

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes disse: "Esta espécie não pode sair por nada, a não ser pela oração."
pt.B: Ele lhes respondeu: "Essa espécie não sai por nenhum outro meio, a não ser pela oração."
pt.R: Jesus respondeu: "Só a oração pode fazer esse tipo de espírito sair."

decisions.choice: by prayer, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "and fasting". The earliest manuscripts lack it. The addition may reflect the growing practice of fasting in the church. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: this kind: this kind of spirit
decisions.reason: Jesus means the kind of spirit that held the boy.

decisions.choice: by prayer: by depending on God
alternatives: by a special prayer said over the boy
decisions.reason: Jesus does not pray aloud in the story. He speaks of the trust in God that prayer expresses, which the disciples lacked (9:19). The words do not explain why this kind needs it more than others.

decisions.choice: this kind of spirit
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind is meant.

source.text: Κἀκεῖθεν ἐξελθόντες παρεπορεύοντο διὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, καὶ οὐκ ἤθελεν ἵνα τις γνοῖ·

records.literal_gloss: And from there having gone out they were passing through Galilee, and not did he want that anyone should know;

en.L: And going out from there, they were passing through Galilee, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not want anyone to know [it];
en.B: They left that place and made their way through Galilee. Jesus did not want anyone to know where they were,
en.R: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers left that area and traveled through Galilee. Jesus did not want people to know where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was,

vi.L: Và rời khỏi nơi đó, họ đi ngang qua Ga-li-lê, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không muốn cho ai biết;
vi.B: Họ rời nơi đó và đi qua miền Ga-li-lê. Đức Giê-xu không muốn ai biết họ đang ở đâu,
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu và các môn đồ rời vùng đó và đi qua miền Ga-li-lê. Đức Giê-xu không muốn người ta biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang ở đâu,

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 거기에서 떠나 갈릴리를 지나가고 있었다. 그리고 그분은 누구든지 [그것을] 아는 것을 원하지 않으셨다.
ko.B: 그들은 그곳을 떠나 갈릴리를 거쳐 갔다. 예수께서는 자기들이 어디 있는지 아무도 알지 못하기를 바라셨다.
ko.R: 예수와 제자들은 그곳을 떠나 갈릴리 지방을 지나갔다. 예수께서는 자기가 어디 계신지 사람들이 알지 못하기를 바라셨다.

es.L: Y saliendo de allí, pasaban por Galilea, y no quería que nadie [lo] supiera;
es.B: Salieron de allí y atravesaron Galilea. Jesús no quería que nadie supiera dónde estaban,
es.R: Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos se fueron de esa región y viajaron por Galilea. Jesús no quería que la gente supiera dónde estaba,

fr.L: Et étant partis de là, ils traversaient la Galilée, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne voulait pas que quelqu’un [le] sache ;
fr.B: Ils quittèrent cet endroit et traversèrent la Galilée. Jésus ne voulait pas qu’on sache où ils étaient,
fr.R: Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples ont quitté cette région et ont traversé la Galilée. Jésus ne voulait pas que les gens sachent où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était,

sw.L: Na wakitoka huko walikuwa wakipita katikati ya Galilaya, naye hakutaka mtu yeyote ajue;
sw.B: Waliondoka mahali pale, wakapita katika Galilaya. Yesu hakutaka mtu yeyote ajue walipo,
sw.R: Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} waliondoka eneo lile, wakasafiri kupitia Galilaya. Yesu hakutaka watu wajue alipo,

pt.L: E, saindo dali, passavam pela Galileia, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} não queria que ninguém [o] soubesse;
pt.B: Eles saíram dali e atravessaram a Galileia. Jesus não queria que ninguém soubesse onde eles estavam,
pt.R: Jesus e os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} seguidores deixaram aquela região e viajaram pela Galileia. Jesus não queria que as pessoas soubessem onde {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} estava,

decisions.choice: passing through: traveling through without stopping to teach the crowds
decisions.reason: The verb means to go along through a place. The journey now leads toward Jerusalem (10:1, 10:32).

decisions.choice: he did not want anyone to know: because he was teaching the disciples
decisions.reason: The next sentence gives the reason: this was a time to teach the Twelve.

decisions.choice: where they were (B); where he was (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what Jesus did not want known.

decisions.choice: "자기가 어디 계신지"
decisions.reason: The narrator honours Jesus even inside a clause about him; "자기" keeps the reflexive of the English "he".

source.text: ἐδίδασκεν γὰρ τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ὅτι Ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων, καὶ ἀποκτενοῦσιν αὐτόν, καὶ ἀποκτανθεὶς μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἀναστήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: he was teaching for the disciples of him and he was saying to them that, The Son of Man is handed over into [the] hands of men, and they will kill him, and having been killed after three days he will arise.

en.L: for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and saying to them, "The Son of Man is handed over into [the] hands of {{gender:people|men}}, and they will kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has been killed, after three days {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rise."
en.B: for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was busy teaching {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples. "The Son of Man is going to be handed over into human hands," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them. "They will kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and three days after {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is killed {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rise again."
en.R: because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers. He said to them, "The Son of Man will be handed over to people who will kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But three days after {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} dies, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will come back to life."

vi.L: vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang dạy các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và nói với họ rằng: "Con Người bị nộp vào tay người ta, và họ sẽ giết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và sau khi bị giết, sau ba ngày {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ sống lại."
vi.B: vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang bận dạy dỗ các môn đồ. Ngài nói với họ: "Con Người sắp bị nộp vào tay loài người. Họ sẽ giết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và ba ngày sau khi bị giết, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ sống lại."
vi.R: vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang dạy các môn đồ. Ngài nói với họ: "Con Người sẽ bị nộp cho những người sẽ giết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Nhưng ba ngày sau khi chết, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ sống lại."

ko.L: 그분이 그분의 제자들을 가르치시며 그들에게 말씀하고 계셨기 때문이다. "인자가 사람들의 손에 넘겨진다. 그리고 그들이 그를 죽일 것이다. 그리고 그는 죽임을 당하고 사흘 후에 살아날 것이다."
ko.B: 예수께서 제자들을 가르치고 계셨기 때문이다. 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "인자는 사람들의 손에 넘겨질 것이다. 그들이 그를 죽일 것이다. 그러나 그는 죽임을 당하고 사흘 뒤에 다시 살아날 것이다."
ko.R: 예수께서 제자들을 가르치고 계셨기 때문이다. 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "인자는 사람들에게 넘겨질 것이다. 그들이 그를 죽일 것이다. 그러나 그는 죽은 지 사흘 뒤에 다시 살아날 것이다."

es.L: porque enseñaba a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y les decía: «El Hijo del Hombre es entregado en manos de {{gender:seres humanos|hombres}}, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} matarán, y una vez muerto, después de tres días resucitará».
es.B: porque estaba dedicado a enseñar a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos. «El Hijo del Hombre va a ser entregado en manos humanas», les decía. «Lo matarán, y tres días después de que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} maten, resucitará».
es.R: porque estaba enseñando a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos. Les dijo: «El Hijo del Hombre será entregado a gente que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} matará. Pero tres días después de morir, volverá a la vida».

fr.L: car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} enseignait {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples et leur disait : « Le Fils de l’homme est livré entre [les] mains {{gender:des humains|des hommes}}, et ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} tueront, et, ayant été tué, après trois jours {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ressuscitera. »
fr.B: car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était occupé à instruire {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples. « Le Fils de l’homme va être livré entre des mains humaines, leur disait-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}. Ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} tueront, et trois jours après avoir été tué, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ressuscitera. »
fr.R: parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} enseignait {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples. Il leur disait : « Le Fils de l’homme va être livré à des gens qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} tueront. Mais trois jours après {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mort, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} reviendra à la vie. »

sw.L: kwa maana alikuwa akiwafundisha wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, na kuwaambia kwamba, "Mwana wa Adamu anakabidhiwa mikononi mwa wanadamu, nao watamwua, na akiisha kuuawa, baada ya siku tatu atafufuka."
sw.B: kwa sababu alikuwa akiwafundisha wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Aliwaambia, "Mwana wa Adamu atakabidhiwa mikononi mwa wanadamu. Watamwua, na siku tatu baada ya kuuawa atafufuka."
sw.R: kwa sababu alikuwa akiwafundisha wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Aliwaambia, "Mwana wa Adamu atakabidhiwa kwa watu watakaomwua. Lakini siku tatu baada ya kufa, atafufuka."

pt.L: pois {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} ensinava os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos e lhes dizia: "O Filho do Homem é entregue nas mãos {{gender:dos seres humanos|dos homens}}, e eles {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} matarão, e, depois de morto, após três dias {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} ressuscitará."
pt.B: pois {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} estava ocupado ensinando os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos. "O Filho do Homem vai ser entregue nas mãos dos seres humanos", {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes dizia. "Eles {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} matarão, e três dias depois de ser morto {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} ressuscitará."
pt.R: porque {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} estava ensinando os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} seguidores. Ele disse a eles: "O Filho do Homem vai ser entregue a pessoas que vão matá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}. Mas três dias depois de morrer, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} vai voltar à vida."

decisions.choice: is handed over: a present tense for something certain and already under way
alternatives: it is happening at this moment
decisions.reason: The present makes the future sure. The verbs that follow are future.

decisions.choice: handed over: delivered up to others
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of Judas handing Jesus over (3:19; 14:10) and of God giving up his servant (Isaiah 53:6 in the Greek). Here the one who hands him over is not named.

decisions.choice: after three days: on the third day
decisions.reason: As in 8:31, the phrase counts parts of days. Mark tells of the rising early on the third day (16:1-2).

decisions.choice: Son of Man ... hands of men: a play on the word for human beings
decisions.reason: The one called the Son of Man is given into the hands of human beings.

decisions.choice: handed over
decisions.reason: All levels say "handed over", since Jesus does not yet speak of Judas and the verb is wider than betrayal.

decisions.choice: "bị nộp" for "handed over", at every level
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 10:33, so the thread of the predictions stays visible.

decisions.choice: "người ta" (L), "loài người" (B) with no gender span
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese words already mean human beings, so the English gender span has no Vietnamese counterpart. "Con Người ... loài người" (B) keeps the play on the word.

decisions.choice: "넘겨지다" at every level
decisions.reason: As in the Korean John (13:21; 18:30): "넘겨주다" keeps the one verb that runs through the passion, from Judas to the chief priests to Pilate. Literal keeps the present "넘겨진다".

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks of the Son of Man as "그", without honorific
decisions.reason: Jesus does not honour himself in his own speech; the narrator's honorific is for the narrator's voice.

decisions.choice: entregado
decisions.reason: As in English "handed over": the same verb is used later of Judas and of the leaders handing Jesus to Pilate, and "entregar" keeps that thread.

decisions.choice: seres humanos / hombres
decisions.reason: The Greek word means human beings; the gender setting gives the traditional "hombres", which also keeps the play on "Hijo del Hombre".

decisions.choice: kukabidhiwa (handed over)
decisions.reason: "Kukabidhiwa" is to be handed over into someone's keeping, the sense the meaning decision gives; "kusalitiwa" would say betrayed, which is only part of it. The same verb in 10:33.

decisions.choice: mikononi mwa wanadamu, no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English Literal
decisions.reason: "Wanadamu" (human beings) already includes women and men, so Swahili has no second wording for the gender setting; the only traditional alternative, "wanaume", would mean males. "Mwana wa Adamu ... wanadamu" also keeps the play on words the meaning decision describes. Throughout the chapter the verb prefix a- (he or she) needs no gender span either.

decisions.choice: {{gender:dos seres humanos|dos homens}}
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 17:22: "seres humanos" keeps the play on "Filho do Homem" (m4) better than "pessoas".

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἠγνόουν τὸ ῥῆμα, καὶ ἐφοβοῦντο αὐτὸν ἐπερωτῆσαι.

records.literal_gloss: But they did not understand the saying, and they were afraid him to ask.

en.L: But they did not understand the saying, and they were afraid to ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: But they did not grasp what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} meant, and they were afraid to question {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: But the disciples did not understand what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} meant, and they were too afraid to ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

vi.L: Nhưng họ không hiểu lời ấy, và sợ không dám hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Nhưng họ không hiểu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} muốn nói gì, và lại sợ không dám hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Nhưng các môn đồ không hiểu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} muốn nói gì, và họ quá sợ nên không dám hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그러나 그들은 그 말씀을 깨닫지 못했고, 그분께 묻기를 두려워했다.
ko.B: 그러나 그들은 예수의 말씀이 무슨 뜻인지 깨닫지 못했고, 예수께 여쭈어보기도 두려워했다.
ko.R: 그러나 제자들은 예수께서 하신 말씀을 알아듣지 못했다. 그런데도 너무 무서워서 예수께 여쭈어보지 못했다.

es.L: Pero ellos no entendían el dicho, y tenían miedo de preguntarle.
es.B: Pero no comprendían lo que quería decir, y tenían miedo de preguntarle.
es.R: Pero los discípulos no entendían lo que quería decir, y tenían demasiado miedo para preguntarle.

fr.L: Mais ils ne comprenaient pas cette parole, et ils craignaient de {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}interroger.
fr.B: Mais ils ne saisissaient pas ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} voulait dire, et ils avaient peur de {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}interroger.
fr.R: Mais les disciples ne comprenaient pas ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} voulait dire, et ils avaient trop peur pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} poser des questions.

sw.L: Lakini wao hawakulielewa neno hilo, nao waliogopa kumwuliza.
sw.B: Lakini hawakuelewa alichomaanisha, na waliogopa kumwuliza.
sw.R: Lakini wanafunzi hawakuelewa alichomaanisha, nao waliogopa sana kumwuliza.

pt.L: Mas eles não entendiam a palavra e tinham medo de {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} perguntar.
pt.B: Mas eles não compreendiam o que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} queria dizer e tinham medo de {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} fazer perguntas.
pt.R: Mas os discípulos não entenderam o que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} quis dizer, e tinham medo demais de perguntar a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}.

decisions.choice: did not understand, were afraid: imperfects, a lasting state
decisions.reason: They went on not understanding and went on being afraid.

decisions.choice: afraid to ask: perhaps afraid of the answer, or of a rebuke like Peter's (8:33)
decisions.reason: Mark does not say why. The last time a disciple questioned this teaching, Jesus rebuked him.

decisions.choice: what he meant
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what they did not understand.

source.text: Καὶ ἦλθον εἰς Καφαρναούμ.

records.literal_gloss: And they came to Capernaum.

en.L: And they came to Capernaum.
en.B: They arrived at Capernaum.
en.R: Then they came to the town of Capernaum.

vi.L: Và họ đến Ca-bê-na-um.
vi.B: Họ về đến Ca-bê-na-um.
vi.R: Rồi họ đến thị trấn Ca-bê-na-um.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 가버나움에 왔다.
ko.B: 그들은 가버나움에 이르렀다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 그들은 가버나움 마을에 왔다.

es.L: Y llegaron a Capernaúm.
es.B: Llegaron a Capernaúm.
es.R: Luego llegaron al pueblo de Capernaúm.

fr.L: Et ils vinrent à Capharnaüm.
fr.B: Ils arrivèrent à Capharnaüm.
fr.R: Puis ils sont arrivés dans la ville de Capharnaüm.

sw.L: Na wakaja Kapernaumu.
sw.B: Wakafika Kapernaumu.
sw.R: Kisha wakafika katika mji wa Kapernaumu.

pt.L: E chegaram a Cafarnaum.
pt.B: Eles chegaram a Cafarnaum.
pt.R: Depois eles chegaram à cidade de Cafarnaum.

decisions.choice: Capernaum: Jesus' base by the lake
decisions.reason: Jesus had made his home there (1:21; 2:1).

decisions.choice: the town of
decisions.reason: Readable says what Capernaum was.

source.text: καὶ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ γενόμενος ἐπηρώτα αὐτούς· Τί ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ διελογίζεσθε;

records.literal_gloss: And in the house having been, he was asking them, What on the way were you discussing?

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was in the house, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "What were you discussing on the way?"
en.B: Once they were inside the house, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "What was it you were debating as we walked?"
en.R: When they were inside the house, Jesus asked {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers, "What were you talking about while we were walking?"

vi.L: Và khi đã ở trong nhà, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hỏi họ: "Các con đã bàn luận điều gì dọc đường?"
vi.B: Khi đã vào trong nhà, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hỏi họ: "Lúc đi đường các con bàn cãi chuyện gì vậy?"
vi.R: Khi đã vào trong nhà, Đức Giê-xu hỏi các môn đồ: "Lúc đi đường các con nói chuyện gì với nhau vậy?"

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 집에 계실 때에 그들에게 물으셨다. "너희가 길에서 무엇을 의논하였느냐?"
ko.B: 집 안에 들어가시자, 예수께서 그들에게 물으셨다. "너희가 길에서 무엇을 가지고 서로 따졌느냐?"
ko.R: 집 안에 들어가셔서 예수께서 제자들에게 물으셨다. "우리가 길을 걸어올 때 너희는 무슨 이야기를 했느냐?"

es.L: Y estando en la casa, les preguntaba: «¿Qué {{plural_you:discutían|discutíais}} en el camino?».
es.B: Una vez dentro de la casa, les preguntó: «¿Qué {{plural_you:venían|veníais}} discutiendo por el camino?».
es.R: Cuando estuvieron dentro de la casa, Jesús les preguntó a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «¿De qué {{plural_you:estaban|estabais}} hablando mientras caminábamos?».

fr.L: Et une fois dans la maison, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur demandait : « De quoi discutiez-vous en chemin ? »
fr.B: Une fois dans la maison, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur demanda : « De quoi débattiez-vous pendant que nous marchions ? »
fr.R: Quand ils ont été dans la maison, Jésus a demandé à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples : « De quoi parliez-vous pendant que nous marchions ? »

sw.L: Na alipokuwa ndani ya nyumba, akawauliza, "Mlikuwa mkijadiliana nini njiani?"
sw.B: Walipokuwa ndani ya nyumba, aliwauliza, "Mlikuwa mkibishana juu ya nini tulipokuwa njiani?"
sw.R: Walipokuwa ndani ya nyumba, Yesu aliwauliza wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, "Mlikuwa mkizungumza nini tulipokuwa tukitembea njiani?"

pt.L: E, estando em casa, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes perguntava: "O que vocês discutiam no caminho?"
pt.B: Quando já estavam em casa, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes perguntou: "O que vocês estavam discutindo enquanto caminhávamos?"
pt.R: Quando já estavam dentro da casa, Jesus perguntou aos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} seguidores: "Sobre o que vocês estavam conversando enquanto a gente andava?"

decisions.choice: the house: a house known to the reader, perhaps Peter's
decisions.reason: The article points to a known house. Simon's house in Capernaum appears in 1:29 and perhaps 2:1.

decisions.choice: discussing: reasoning together, debating
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 8:16-17. The next sentence shows what the debate was.

decisions.choice: the way: the road they traveled
decisions.reason: The word means road. Mark often places teaching "on the way" to Jerusalem (8:27; 10:32).

decisions.choice: What was it you were debating as we walked? (B); while we were walking (R)
alternatives: What were you discussing on the way?
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "on the way" into a clause.

decisions.choice: enquanto a gente andava
decisions.reason: Readable uses "a gente" for "we", the ordinary Brazilian form in speech, since Jesus is talking with his friends; Balanced keeps "caminhávamos".

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἐσιώπων, πρὸς ἀλλήλους γὰρ διελέχθησαν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ τίς μείζων.

records.literal_gloss: But they were silent; with one another for they had been discussing on the road who [was] greater.

en.L: But they were silent, for on the road they had been discussing with one another who [was] the greatest.
en.B: They said nothing, because on the way they had been debating among themselves which of them was the greatest.
en.R: But they did not answer. They had been arguing with each other on the road about which one of them was the most important.

vi.L: Nhưng họ im lặng, vì dọc đường họ đã bàn luận với nhau xem ai [là] lớn nhất.
vi.B: Họ đều im lặng, vì dọc đường họ đã tranh luận với nhau xem ai là người lớn nhất.
vi.R: Nhưng họ không trả lời. Vì dọc đường họ đã cãi nhau xem ai trong họ là người quan trọng nhất.

ko.L: 그러나 그들은 잠잠했다. 그들이 길에서 누가 더 큰지 서로 의논했기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그들은 아무 말도 하지 않았다. 길에서 자기들 가운데 누가 가장 큰 사람인지 서로 따졌기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그러나 제자들은 대답하지 않았다. 길에서 자기들 가운데 누가 가장 높은 사람인지를 두고 서로 다투었기 때문이다.

es.L: Pero ellos callaban, porque en el camino habían discutido entre sí quién [era] el mayor.
es.B: Ellos guardaron silencio, porque por el camino habían estado discutiendo entre ellos quién era el mayor.
es.R: Pero no respondieron. En el camino habían estado discutiendo entre ellos sobre quién era el más importante.

fr.L: Mais ils se taisaient, car en chemin ils avaient discuté entre eux [pour savoir] qui [était] le plus grand.
fr.B: Ils gardèrent le silence, car en chemin ils s’étaient demandé entre eux lequel était le plus grand.
fr.R: Mais ils n’ont pas répondu. Sur la route, ils s’étaient disputés pour savoir lequel d’entre eux était le plus important.

sw.L: Lakini wao wakanyamaza, kwa maana njiani walikuwa wamejadiliana wao kwa wao ni nani aliye mkuu [zaidi].
sw.B: Wakanyamaza kimya, kwa sababu njiani walikuwa wakibishana wao kwa wao ni nani kati yao aliye mkuu kuliko wote.
sw.R: Lakini hawakujibu. Njiani walikuwa wakibishana wao kwa wao ni nani kati yao aliye muhimu kuliko wote.

pt.L: Mas eles ficaram calados, pois no caminho tinham discutido uns com os outros sobre quem [era] o maior.
pt.B: Eles não disseram nada, porque no caminho tinham discutido entre si qual deles era o maior.
pt.R: Mas eles não responderam. No caminho, eles tinham discutido uns com os outros sobre qual deles era o mais importante.

decisions.choice: greater: the form meaning greater, used here for greatest
decisions.reason: Greek of this time often used the form for "greater" to mean the greatest of a group.

decisions.choice: who: which one of them
decisions.reason: They were comparing themselves with each other.

decisions.choice: they were silent: they kept quiet out of shame
decisions.reason: Their silence follows Jesus' teaching about his death (9:31).

decisions.choice: the most important
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday phrase for greatness in rank.

decisions.choice: "더 큰" (L); "가장 큰" (B); "가장 높은" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek form means "greater", used for "greatest" (meaning decision); Literal keeps the comparative, which Korean can bear here.

source.text: καὶ καθίσας ἐφώνησεν τοὺς δώδεκα καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Εἴ τις θέλει πρῶτος εἶναι ἔσται πάντων ἔσχατος καὶ πάντων διάκονος.

records.literal_gloss: And having sat down he called the twelve and says to them, If anyone desires first to be, he will be of all last and of all servant.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat down and called the twelve and says to them, "If anyone wants to be first, {{gender:they|he}} will be last of all and servant of all."
en.B: He sat down, called the Twelve, and said to them, "Whoever wants to be first must be last of everyone and the servant of everyone."
