en.R: Jesus sat down and called the Twelve to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He said, "If you want to be the most important, you must put yourself last. You must serve everyone else."

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngồi xuống, gọi [nhóm] Mười Hai, và nói với họ: "Nếu ai muốn làm người đứng đầu, người ấy sẽ là người cuối cùng của mọi người và là người phục vụ mọi người."
vi.B: Ngài ngồi xuống, gọi nhóm Mười Hai lại và nói với họ: "Ai muốn đứng đầu thì phải làm người cuối cùng hết, và làm người phục vụ mọi người."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu ngồi xuống và gọi mười hai môn đồ đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Ngài nói: "Nếu các con muốn làm người quan trọng nhất, các con phải tự đặt mình ở chỗ thấp nhất. Các con phải phục vụ mọi người."

ko.L: 그리고 그분은 앉으셔서 열둘을 부르시고 그들에게 말씀하신다. "누구든지 첫째가 되고 싶으면, 모든 사람 가운데 꼴찌가 되고 모든 사람을 섬기는 사람이 될 것이다."
ko.B: 예수께서 앉으셔서 열두 제자를 부르시고 말씀하셨다. "누구든지 첫째가 되려는 사람은 모든 사람의 꼴찌가 되고, 모든 사람을 섬기는 사람이 되어야 한다."
ko.R: 예수께서 앉으셔서 열두 제자를 부르셨다. 그리고 말씀하셨다. "가장 높은 사람이 되고 싶으면, 너 자신을 맨 뒤에 두어야 한다. 다른 모든 사람을 섬겨야 한다."

es.L: Y sentándose, llamó a los doce y les dice: «Si alguno quiere ser primero, será el último de todos y servidor de todos».
es.B: Se sentó, llamó a los Doce y les dijo: «El que quiera ser el primero, que sea el último de todos y el servidor de todos».
es.R: Jesús se sentó y llamó a los Doce. Les dijo: «Si alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} quiere ser el más importante, tiene que ponerse en el último lugar. Tiene que servir a todos los demás».

fr.L: Et s’étant assis, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} appela les Douze et leur dit : « Si quelqu’un veut être le premier, il sera le dernier de tous et le serviteur de tous. »
fr.B: Il s’assit, appela les Douze et leur dit : « Celui qui veut être le premier doit être le dernier de tous et le serviteur de tous. »
fr.R: Jésus s’est assis et a appelé les Douze près de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Il leur a dit : « Si vous voulez être les plus importants, vous devez vous mettre à la dernière place. Vous devez servir tous les autres. »

sw.L: Naye akaketi, akawaita wale Kumi na Wawili, na anawaambia, "Mtu yeyote akitaka kuwa wa kwanza, atakuwa wa mwisho wa wote na mtumishi wa wote."
sw.B: Akaketi, akawaita wale Kumi na Wawili, akawaambia, "Mtu yeyote anayetaka kuwa wa kwanza lazima awe wa mwisho kuliko wote na mtumishi wa wote."
sw.R: Yesu aliketi, akawaita wale Kumi na Wawili waje {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}. Akawaambia, "Mtu yeyote akitaka kuwa muhimu kuliko wote, lazima ajiweke wa mwisho. Lazima awahudumie wengine wote."

pt.L: E, sentando-se, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} chamou os doze e lhes diz: "Se alguém quer ser o primeiro, será o último de todos e o servo de todos."
pt.B: Ele se sentou, chamou os Doze e lhes disse: "Quem quiser ser o primeiro deve ser o último de todos e o servo de todos."
pt.R: Jesus se sentou e chamou os Doze para perto {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}. Ele disse: "Se vocês querem ser os mais importantes, precisam se colocar em último lugar. Precisam servir a todos os outros."

decisions.choice: sat down: the posture of a teacher
decisions.reason: Teachers sat to teach (4:1). The words that follow are formal teaching.

decisions.choice: he will be: a future that works as a command
alternatives: a warning that he will end up last
decisions.reason: The future can state what must be. It could also mean that whoever seeks first place will be put last.

decisions.choice: servant: one who serves others, as at table
decisions.reason: The word is the one for a servant who waits on others. Mark uses the word for slave in 10:44.

decisions.choice: says: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again.

decisions.choice: If you want to be the most important, you must put yourself last
alternatives: If anyone desires to be first
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to the hearer directly and says what "first" means.

decisions.choice: "[nhóm] Mười Hai" (L), "nhóm Mười Hai" (B), "mười hai môn đồ" (R)
decisions.reason: As John 6:67 and 20:24.

decisions.choice: "người phục vụ" for the servant (diakonos)
decisions.reason: "đầy tớ" stays for the Greek word for slave at Balanced and Readable; this word is one who waits on others, and it links to 10:43-45.

decisions.choice: "ai ... người ấy" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese words are already inclusive.

decisions.choice: "섬기는 사람" for diakonos
decisions.reason: The servant is one who serves others, as at table (meaning decision); "섬기는 사람" says that and leaves "종" for doulos (10:44). No gender span: "누구든지" already includes everyone.

decisions.choice: servidor
decisions.reason: One who serves others, as at table (meaning decision). Spanish keeps "servidor" for this word and "esclavo" for the stronger word in 10:44, so the two stay apart.

decisions.choice: no gender setting
decisions.reason: Spanish needs no pronoun here ("será el último"), so the English gender setting has nothing to apply to.

decisions.choice: Si quelqu’un veut ..., il sera (L), with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span on the pronoun, as the English Literal has
decisions.reason: French "quelqu’un" already means anyone, and the "il" that refers back to it is ordinary generic French, so no gender setting is needed where the English has one for the pronoun (French guide, section 7). The same holds in 9:41 and 9:42.

decisions.choice: mtumishi (servant)
decisions.reason: "Mtumishi" is one who serves others, the sense the meaning decision gives for this word (one who serves, as at table). It is kept apart from "mtumwa" (slave), which Mark sets beside it in 10:43-44.

decisions.choice: será, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English needs a pronoun after "anyone" and so a setting. Portuguese leaves the subject of "será" unexpressed, and "alguém" already means anyone, so no setting is needed (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 7).

source.text: καὶ λαβὼν παιδίον ἔστησεν αὐτὸ ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν καὶ ἐναγκαλισάμενος αὐτὸ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς·

records.literal_gloss: And having taken a child he set it in [the] midst of them, and having taken in arms it he said to them,

en.L: And taking a child, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} set it in the middle of them, and taking it in [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] arms, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them,
en.B: He took a little child and stood the child among them. Then, putting {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} arms around the child, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them,
en.R: Then Jesus took a little child and had the child stand in front of them. He took the child in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} arms and said to them,

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lấy một đứa trẻ, đặt nó đứng giữa họ, và ôm nó vào lòng, rồi nói với họ:
vi.B: Ngài dẫn một em nhỏ đến, cho em đứng giữa họ. Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ôm em vào lòng và nói với họ:
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu đem một em nhỏ đến và cho em đứng trước mặt các môn đồ. Ngài ôm em vào lòng và nói với họ:

ko.L: 그리고 그분은 어린아이 하나를 데려다가 그들 가운데 세우시고, 그 아이를 [팔에] 안으시며 그들에게 말씀하셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서 어린아이 하나를 데려다가 그들 가운데 세우시고, 그 아이를 품에 안으시며 그들에게 말씀하셨다.
ko.R: 그리고 예수께서 어린아이 하나를 데려와 제자들 앞에 세우셨다. 그리고 그 아이를 품에 안으시고 말씀하셨다.

es.L: Y tomando a un niño, lo puso en medio de ellos, y tomándolo en [{{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}}] brazos, les dijo:
es.B: Tomó a un niño pequeño y lo puso en medio de ellos. Luego lo abrazó y les dijo:
es.R: Entonces Jesús tomó a un niño pequeño y lo puso de pie delante de ellos. Tomó al niño en {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} brazos y les dijo:

fr.L: Et prenant un petit enfant, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le plaça au milieu d’eux, et l’ayant pris dans [{{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}}] bras, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit :
fr.B: Il prit un petit enfant et le plaça au milieu d’eux ; puis, le serrant dans {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} bras, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit :
fr.R: Puis Jésus a pris un petit enfant et l’a placé devant eux. Il l’a pris dans {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} bras et leur a dit :

sw.L: Na akitwaa mtoto, akamsimamisha katikati yao, na akimkumbatia, akawaambia,
sw.B: Akamchukua mtoto mdogo, akamsimamisha katikati yao. Kisha akamkumbatia, akawaambia,
sw.R: Kisha Yesu alimchukua mtoto mdogo, akamsimamisha mbele yao. Akamkumbatia, akawaambia,

pt.L: E, tomando uma criança, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} a colocou no meio deles e, tomando-a nos [{{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}}] braços, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes disse:
pt.B: Ele pegou uma criança pequena e a pôs de pé no meio deles. Depois, abraçando a criança, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes disse:
pt.R: Então Jesus pegou uma criança pequena e a fez ficar de pé na frente deles. Ele pegou a criança nos braços e disse a eles:

decisions.choice: a child: someone with no rank or importance
decisions.reason: Children had no standing in that society. Jesus answers the debate about greatness by setting one in the middle.

decisions.choice: taking in his arms: embracing
decisions.reason: The verb means to hold in the arms. Mark uses it again in 10:16.

decisions.choice: it: the word for child is neuter
decisions.reason: Mark does not say whether the child was a boy or a girl.

decisions.choice: the child
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable avoid calling a child "it".

decisions.choice: "em nhỏ", "em" for the child (B, R); "đứa trẻ", "nó" (L)
decisions.reason: "em" is the warm, ordinary word for a young child; Literal keeps the plain noun and pronoun.

decisions.choice: [팔에]
decisions.reason: The Greek verb alone means to take in one's arms; Literal brackets the arms that Korean names.

decisions.choice: uma criança ... a
decisions.reason: "Criança" is feminine in grammar but says nothing of sex, like the Greek neuter (m3), so Portuguese can call the child "a" at every level without the problem the English avoids.

source.text: Ὃς ἂν ἓν τῶν τοιούτων παιδίων δέξηται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου, ἐμὲ δέχεται· καὶ ὃς ἂν ἐμὲ δέχηται, οὐκ ἐμὲ δέχεται ἀλλὰ τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με.

records.literal_gloss: Whoever one of such little children shall receive in the name of me, me receives; and whoever me shall receive, not me receives but the [One] having sent me.

en.L: "Whoever receives one of such children in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name receives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; and whoever receives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} receives not {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} but the One who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.B: "Whoever welcomes a child like this one in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is welcoming {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. And whoever welcomes {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is welcoming, not {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, but the One who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.R: "When someone welcomes a little child like this for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sake, they are welcoming {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. And when they welcome {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, they are not only welcoming {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They are also welcoming God, who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

vi.L: "Ai nhân danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} tiếp nhận một trong những đứa trẻ như thế này là tiếp nhận {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; và ai tiếp nhận {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì không phải tiếp nhận {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, nhưng [tiếp nhận] Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.B: "Ai nhân danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} mà tiếp đón một em nhỏ như em này là tiếp đón {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Và ai tiếp đón {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì không phải là tiếp đón {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, nhưng là tiếp đón Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.R: "Khi ai vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} mà tiếp đón một em nhỏ như em này, người ấy tiếp đón {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Và khi tiếp đón {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, người ấy không chỉ tiếp đón {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} mà thôi. Người ấy cũng tiếp đón Đức Chúa Trời, Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."

ko.L: "누구든지 내 이름으로 이런 어린아이들 가운데 하나를 영접하면 나를 영접하는 것이다. 그리고 누구든지 나를 영접하면, 나를 영접하는 것이 아니라 나를 보내신 분을 영접하는 것이다."
ko.B: "누구든지 내 이름으로 이런 어린아이 하나를 맞아들이면 나를 맞아들이는 것이다. 그리고 누구든지 나를 맞아들이면, 나를 맞아들이는 것이 아니라 나를 보내신 분을 맞아들이는 것이다."
ko.R: "누구든지 나를 위해서 이런 어린아이 하나를 반갑게 맞아 주면, 그것은 나를 맞아 주는 것이다. 또 나를 맞아 주는 사람은 나만 맞아 주는 것이 아니다. 나를 보내신 하나님을 맞아 주는 것이다."

es.L: «El que reciba a uno de tales niños en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre, a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} recibe; y el que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} reciba a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} recibe a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, sino al que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió».
es.B: «El que recibe en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre a un niño como este, a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} recibe. Y el que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} recibe a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} recibe a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, sino al que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió».
es.R: «Cuando alguien recibe a un niño pequeño como este por amor a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} está recibiendo a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Y cuando alguien {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} recibe a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, no solo {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} recibe a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. También recibe a Dios, que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió».

fr.L: « Quiconque reçoit un de ces petits enfants en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} reçoit ; et quiconque {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} reçoit, ce n’est pas {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qu’il reçoit, mais celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé. »
fr.B: « Celui qui accueille un enfant comme celui-ci en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}accueille. Et celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}accueille, ce n’est pas {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qu’il accueille, mais celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé. »
fr.R: « Quand quelqu’un accueille un petit enfant comme celui-ci à cause de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qu’il accueille. Et quand il {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}accueille, il n’accueille pas seulement {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Il accueille aussi Dieu, qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé. »

sw.L: "Yeyote atakayempokea mmoja wa watoto kama hawa kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, ananipokea {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}; na yeyote atakayenipokea {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, hanipokei {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, bali yule aliyenituma."
sw.B: "Yeyote anayemkaribisha mtoto kama huyu kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} ananikaribisha {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}. Na yeyote anayenikaribisha {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, si {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} anayemkaribisha, bali ni yule aliyenituma."
sw.R: "Mtu anapomkaribisha mtoto mdogo kama huyu kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, ananikaribisha {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}. Na anaponikaribisha {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, hanikaribishi {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} peke {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Anamkaribisha pia Mungu, aliyenituma."

pt.L: "Quem receber uma destas crianças em {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} nome recebe a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}; e quem receber a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} não recebe a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, mas Aquele que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} enviou."
pt.B: "Quem acolhe uma criança como esta em {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} nome está acolhendo a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}. E quem {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} acolhe não está acolhendo a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, mas Aquele que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} enviou."
pt.R: "Quando alguém recebe bem uma criança como esta por causa de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, está recebendo a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}. E, quando alguém {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} recebe, não está recebendo só a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}. Está recebendo também a Deus, que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} enviou."

decisions.choice: in my name: for my sake, because the child belongs to me
alternatives: using my name as a formula
decisions.reason: To do something in someone's name is to do it on their account.

decisions.choice: not me but the one who sent me: not only me but also God
alternatives: they do not receive Jesus at all
decisions.reason: "Not this but that" is a common way of putting stress on the second item. Receiving Jesus is receiving God.

decisions.choice: receive: welcome as a guest
decisions.reason: The verb is used for showing hospitality (6:11).

decisions.choice: the One who sent me: God
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of himself as sent by the Father, as in 12:6.

decisions.choice: for my sake; not only ... also; God
alternatives: in my name; not me but the One who sent me
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idioms and names God as the sender.

decisions.choice: "tiếp nhận" (L); "tiếp đón" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "tiếp đón" is the word for welcoming a guest, which the meaning decision gives as the sense.

decisions.choice: "영접하다" (L); "맞아들이다" (B); "반갑게 맞아 주다" (R)
decisions.reason: To receive is to welcome as a guest (meaning decision); Literal keeps the church word, Balanced and Readable use the everyday words for welcoming someone into the house. Readable names God and says "not only", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: kupokea (L); kukaribisha (B, R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says to receive as a guest. "Kukaribisha" is the Swahili word for welcoming a guest; Literal keeps "kupokea" (receive), the plain counterpart of the Greek verb.

source.text: Ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰωάννης· Διδάσκαλε, εἴδομέν τινα ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου ἐκβάλλοντα δαιμόνια, καὶ ἐκωλύομεν αὐτόν, ὅτι οὐκ ἠκολούθει ἡμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Said to him John, Teacher, we saw someone in the name of you casting out demons, and we were forbidding him, because not he was following us.

en.L: John said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, and we tried to stop him, because he was not following us."
en.B: John said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, we saw a man throwing out demons in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name. We tried to stop him, since he did not go around with us."
en.R: John said to Jesus, "Teacher, we saw a man using {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name to force demons to leave people. We told him to stop, because he was not one of our group."

vi.L: Giăng nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa Thầy, chúng con thấy một người nhân danh Thầy đuổi quỷ, và chúng con đã ngăn cản người ấy, vì người ấy không theo chúng con."
vi.B: Giăng thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa Thầy, chúng con thấy một người nhân danh Thầy mà đuổi quỷ. Chúng con đã tìm cách ngăn cản người ấy, vì người ấy không đi theo chúng con."
vi.R: Giăng thưa với Đức Giê-xu: "Thưa Thầy, chúng con thấy một người dùng danh Thầy để đuổi quỷ ra khỏi người ta. Chúng con bảo người ấy phải ngưng lại, vì người ấy không ở trong nhóm của chúng con."

ko.L: 요한이 그분께 말했다. "선생님, 어떤 사람이 선생님의 이름으로 귀신들을 쫓아내는 것을 저희가 보았습니다. 그리고 그가 저희를 따르지 않았기 때문에 저희가 그를 막으려고 했습니다."
ko.B: 요한이 예수께 말했다. "선생님, 어떤 사람이 선생님의 이름으로 귀신을 쫓아내는 것을 저희가 보았습니다. 그런데 그 사람이 저희와 함께 다니지 않기에 저희가 그를 막으려고 했습니다."
ko.R: 요한이 예수께 말했다. "선생님, 어떤 사람이 선생님의 이름을 써서 사람들에게서 귀신을 쫓아내는 것을 저희가 보았습니다. 그 사람은 저희 무리가 아니어서, 저희가 그러지 말라고 했습니다."

es.L: Juan {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Maestro, vimos a uno que expulsaba demonios en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre, y se lo impedíamos, porque no nos seguía».
es.B: Juan {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Maestro, vimos a un hombre que expulsaba demonios en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre, y tratamos de impedírselo, porque no andaba con nosotros».
es.R: Juan {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo a Jesús: «Maestro, vimos a un hombre que usaba {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre para hacer que los demonios salieran de la gente. Le dijimos que no lo hiciera, porque no era de nuestro grupo».

fr.L: Jean {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Maître, nous avons vu quelqu’un qui chassait des démons en {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom, et nous voulions l’en empêcher, parce qu’il ne nous suivait pas. »
fr.B: Jean {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Maître, nous avons vu un homme chasser des démons en {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom. Nous avons essayé de l’en empêcher, parce qu’il ne venait pas avec nous. »
fr.R: Jean a dit à Jésus : « Maître, nous avons vu un homme qui se servait de {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom pour faire sortir des démons des gens. Nous lui avons dit d’arrêter, parce qu’il ne faisait pas partie de notre groupe. »

sw.L: Yohana akamwambia, "Mwalimu, tulimwona mtu akitoa pepo kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}, nasi tulikuwa tukimzuia, kwa sababu hakuwa akitufuata."
sw.B: Yohana akamwambia, "Mwalimu, tulimwona mtu akifukuza pepo kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}. Tukajaribu kumzuia, kwa kuwa yeye hakuwa anatembea pamoja nasi."
sw.R: Yohana akamwambia Yesu, "Mwalimu, tulimwona mtu akitumia jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} kuwafukuza pepo kutoka kwa watu. Tukamwambia aache, kwa sababu yeye si mmoja wa kundi letu."

pt.L: João {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} disse: "Mestre, vimos alguém expulsando demônios em {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} nome, e tentamos impedi-lo, porque ele não nos seguia."
pt.B: João {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} disse: "Mestre, vimos um homem expulsando demônios em {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} nome. Tentamos impedi-lo, porque ele não andava com a gente."
pt.R: João disse a Jesus: "Mestre, vimos um homem usando o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} nome para fazer demônios saírem das pessoas. Mandamos que ele parasse, porque ele não era do nosso grupo."

decisions.choice: we were forbidding: we tried to stop him
decisions.reason: The imperfect can describe an attempt. It is not clear whether the man obeyed.

decisions.choice: in your name: calling on Jesus' name to drive out demons
decisions.reason: Exorcists used the names of powerful figures. Acts 19:13 tells of men who tried using the name of Jesus.

decisions.choice: following us: not one of the disciples' company
decisions.reason: John says "us", not "you". The concern is about belonging to their group.

decisions.choice: the wording of the SBLGNT
alternatives: add: who does not follow us
decisions.reason: Later manuscripts add "who does not follow us" after "demons" and vary the order of the clauses. The meaning is not changed. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: throwing out (B); force to leave people (R)
decisions.reason: The pattern of earlier chapters.

decisions.choice: "đuổi quỷ" for casting out demons, at every level
decisions.reason: "quỷ" is the word used for demons in John (10:20-21).

decisions.choice: exclusive "chúng con" for "us"
decisions.reason: John means the disciples' own company, set apart from the man; in 9:40 Jesus answers with inclusive "chúng ta".

decisions.choice: "귀신" and "쫓아내다"
decisions.reason: As in Mark 3 and the Korean John (8:48; 10:20): "귀신" for daimonion, keeping "마귀" for the devil.

decisions.choice: pepo (demons); kutoa (L), kufukuza (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Pepo" is the ordinary Swahili word for demons, as in John 10:20-21; "mashetani" would confuse them with Satan. "Kutoa pepo" (bring out) is the usual expression at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "kufukuza" (drive out), as the English says "throwing out".

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Μὴ κωλύετε αὐτόν, οὐδεὶς γάρ ἐστιν ὃς ποιήσει δύναμιν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου καὶ δυνήσεται ταχὺ κακολογῆσαί με·

records.literal_gloss: But Jesus said, Not forbid him, no one for there is who will do a work of power in the name of me and will be able readily to speak evil of me;

en.L: But Jesus said, "Do not stop him, for there is no one who will do a work of power in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name and be able soon afterward to speak evil of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}};
en.B: Jesus said, "Do not stop him. No one who does a mighty work in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name will be quick to speak ill of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} afterward.
en.R: But Jesus said, "Do not stop him. A person who does a powerful miracle by using {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name will not soon turn around and say bad things about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

vi.L: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu nói: "Đừng ngăn cản người ấy, vì không có ai làm một việc quyền năng nhân danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} mà rồi ngay sau đó lại có thể nói xấu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}};
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nói: "Đừng ngăn cản người ấy. Không ai đã nhân danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm việc quyền năng mà lại có thể vội quay ra nói xấu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu nói: "Đừng ngăn cản người ấy. Ai dùng danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} để làm phép lạ thì sẽ không quay lại nói xấu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ngay được.

ko.L: 그러나 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "그를 막지 마라. 내 이름으로 능력 있는 일을 행하고 나서 곧 나를 나쁘게 말할 수 있는 사람은 없기 때문이다.
ko.B: 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "그를 막지 마라. 내 이름으로 기적을 행하는 사람이 곧이어 나를 헐뜯을 수는 없다.
ko.R: 그러나 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "그 사람을 막지 마라. 내 이름을 써서 놀라운 일을 하는 사람이, 금방 돌아서서 나를 나쁘게 말하지는 못한다.

es.L: Pero Jesús dijo: «No se lo {{plural_you:impidan|impidáis}}, porque no hay nadie que haga una obra poderosa en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre y pueda poco después hablar mal de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}};
es.B: Jesús dijo: «No se lo {{plural_you:impidan|impidáis}}. Nadie que haga un milagro en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre podrá luego hablar mal de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} tan fácilmente.
es.R: Pero Jesús dijo: «No se lo {{plural_you:impidan|impidáis}}. Una persona que hace un milagro usando {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre no va a ponerse enseguida a decir cosas malas de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

fr.L: Mais Jésus dit : « Ne l’en empêchez pas, car il n’y a personne qui fera une œuvre de puissance en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom et qui pourra aussitôt après dire du mal de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ;
fr.B: Jésus répondit : « Ne l’en empêchez pas. Personne ne peut accomplir une œuvre puissante en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom et se mettre aussitôt après à dire du mal de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: Mais Jésus a dit : « Ne l’en empêchez pas. Celui qui fait un grand miracle en se servant de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom ne va pas, juste après, dire du mal de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.

sw.L: Lakini Yesu akasema, "Msimzuie, kwa maana hakuna mtu atakayefanya tendo la nguvu kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, kisha akaweza upesi kunisema vibaya;
sw.B: Yesu akasema, "Msimzuie. Hakuna mtu anayefanya tendo kuu kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} ambaye atakuwa mwepesi kunisema vibaya baadaye.
sw.R: Lakini Yesu akasema, "Msimzuie. Mtu anayefanya muujiza mkubwa kwa kutumia jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} hatageuka upesi na kunisema vibaya.

pt.L: Mas Jesus disse: "Não o impeçam, pois não há ninguém que faça um milagre em {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} nome e possa logo depois falar mal de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}};
pt.B: Jesus disse: "Não o impeçam. Ninguém que faz um milagre em {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} nome vai depressa falar mal de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}.
pt.R: Mas Jesus disse: "Não o impeçam. Uma pessoa que faz um milagre usando o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} nome não vai logo depois mudar de lado e falar mal de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}.

decisions.choice: do not stop him: a present command, stop trying to prevent him
decisions.reason: The form tells them to give up what they were doing.

decisions.choice: soon afterward: quickly, readily
decisions.reason: The adverb means quickly. A man who has just done a mighty deed in Jesus' name will not turn at once to speak against him.

decisions.choice: work of power: a miracle
decisions.reason: The same word as in 6:2 and 6:5.

decisions.choice: will not soon turn around and say bad things about me
alternatives: will be able readily to speak evil of me
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for the idiom.

decisions.choice: "việc quyền năng" (L, B); "phép lạ" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is "power"; Literal and Balanced keep it. Readable says "phép lạ" (miracle), which John's "sign" never takes, because here the word is not "sign".

decisions.choice: "능력 있는 일" (L); "기적" (B); "놀라운 일" (R)
decisions.reason: A work of power is a miracle (meaning decision); Literal keeps "power" in the phrase, Balanced and Readable say what it was.

source.text: ὃς γὰρ οὐκ ἔστιν καθ’ ἡμῶν, ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: whoever for not is against us, for us is.

en.L: for whoever is not against us is for us.
en.B: Anyone not against us is for us.
en.R: If people are not against us, they are on our side.

vi.L: vì ai không chống lại chúng ta là ủng hộ chúng ta.
vi.B: Ai không chống lại chúng ta là ở về phía chúng ta.
vi.R: Nếu người ta không chống lại chúng ta, thì họ đứng về phía chúng ta.

ko.L: 우리를 반대하지 않는 사람은 우리를 위하는 사람이기 때문이다.
ko.B: 우리를 반대하지 않는 사람은 우리 편이다.
ko.R: 우리를 반대하지 않는 사람은 우리 편에 서 있는 사람이다.

es.L: porque el que no está contra nosotros, por nosotros está.
es.B: El que no está contra nosotros está a nuestro favor.
es.R: Si alguien no está en contra de nosotros, está de nuestro lado.

fr.L: car celui qui n’est pas contre nous est pour nous.
fr.B: Celui qui n’est pas contre nous est pour nous.
fr.R: Si des gens ne sont pas contre nous, ils sont avec nous.

sw.L: kwa maana yeyote asiye kinyume chetu yuko upande wetu.
sw.B: Yeyote asiyepingana nasi yuko upande wetu.
sw.R: Watu wasiotupinga wako upande wetu.

pt.L: pois quem não é contra nós é por nós.
pt.B: Quem não é contra nós está a nosso favor.
pt.R: Quem não está contra nós está do nosso lado.

decisions.choice: us, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "against you ... for you". The SBLGNT reads "us", which includes Jesus with his disciples. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: not against us is for us: a generous rule for those who act in Jesus' name
decisions.reason: Matthew 12:30 gives the reverse: whoever is not with me is against me. There Jesus speaks of those who oppose him; here of one who acts in his name.

decisions.choice: on our side
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday phrase.

decisions.choice: inclusive "chúng ta" for "us"
decisions.reason: Jesus counts himself with his disciples, answering John's exclusive "chúng con" in 9:38.

source.text: Ὃς γὰρ ἂν ποτίσῃ ὑμᾶς ποτήριον ὕδατος ἐν ὀνόματι ὅτι χριστοῦ ἐστε, ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ ἀπολέσῃ τὸν μισθὸν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Whoever for might give to drink you a cup of water in name that of Christ you are, truly I say to you that no not shall he lose the reward of him.

en.L: For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink in [the] name that you belong to the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, truly I say to you that {{gender:they|he}} will by no means lose {{gender:their|his}} reward.
en.B: If anyone gives you a cup of water to drink because you belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, truly I tell you, that person will certainly not lose the reward.
en.R: I tell you the truth: if someone gives you so much as a cup of water because you belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, God will surely reward that person.

vi.L: Vì ai cho các con uống một chén nước nhân danh [rằng] các con thuộc về {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, người ấy chắc chắn không mất phần thưởng của mình.
vi.B: Ai cho các con uống một chén nước vì các con thuộc về {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, người ấy chắc chắn sẽ không mất phần thưởng của mình.
vi.R: Ta nói thật với các con: nếu ai cho các con dù chỉ một chén nước vì các con thuộc về {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, Đức Chúa Trời chắc chắn sẽ ban thưởng cho người ấy.

ko.L: 누구든지 너희가 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}에게 속한 사람이라는 이유로 너희에게 물 한 잔을 마시게 하면, 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 그는 결코 자기 상을 잃지 않을 것이다.
ko.B: 너희가 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}에게 속한 사람이라고 해서 누가 너희에게 물 한 잔이라도 마시게 하면, 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 그 사람은 결코 상을 잃지 않을 것이다.
ko.R: 내가 분명히 말한다. 너희가 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}에게 속한 사람이라고 해서 누가 너희에게 물 한 잔이라도 준다면, 하나님께서 그 사람에게 꼭 상을 주실 것이다.

es.L: Porque cualquiera que {{plural_you:les|os}} dé a beber un vaso de agua en [el] nombre de que {{plural_you:son|sois}} {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}, en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que de ningún modo perderá su recompensa.
es.B: Si alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} da a beber un vaso de agua porque {{plural_you:son|sois}} {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}, en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que esa persona no se quedará sin su recompensa.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: si alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} da aunque sea un vaso de agua porque {{plural_you:pertenecen|pertenecéis}} {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}, Dios le dará con seguridad su recompensa.

fr.L: Car quiconque vous donnera à boire une coupe d’eau au nom [du fait] que vous êtes au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, en vérité, je vous le dis, il ne perdra pas sa récompense.
fr.B: Si quelqu’un vous donne un verre d’eau à boire parce que vous appartenez au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, en vérité, je vous le dis, il ne perdra certainement pas sa récompense.
fr.R: Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité : si quelqu’un vous donne ne serait-ce qu’un verre d’eau parce que vous appartenez au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, Dieu le récompensera, c’est certain.

sw.L: Kwa maana yeyote atakayewapa kikombe cha maji mnywe kwa jina, kwa sababu ninyi ni wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, kweli nawaambia kwamba hatapoteza kamwe thawabu yake.
sw.B: Mtu yeyote atakayewapa kikombe cha maji mnywe kwa sababu ninyi ni wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, kweli nawaambia, mtu huyo hatakosa kamwe thawabu yake.
sw.R: Nawaambia ukweli: mtu akiwapa hata kikombe cha maji tu kwa sababu ninyi ni wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, hakika Mungu atampa thawabu.

pt.L: Pois quem lhes der de beber um copo de água em nome de [que] vocês são {{christos:de Cristo|do Messias}}, em verdade eu lhes digo que de modo nenhum perderá a sua recompensa.
pt.B: Se alguém lhes der um copo de água para beber porque vocês pertencem {{christos:a Cristo|ao Messias}}, em verdade eu lhes digo: essa pessoa certamente não perderá a recompensa.
pt.R: Eu garanto a vocês: se alguém der a vocês nem que seja um copo de água porque vocês pertencem {{christos:a Cristo|ao Messias}}, Deus com certeza vai recompensar essa pessoa.

decisions.choice: in name that you are Christ's: because you belong to Christ
decisions.reason: The phrase means on the ground that, or because. The gift is given to the disciples as Christ's people.

decisions.choice: Christ: the Messiah, God's anointed king
decisions.reason: Jesus rarely uses the title of himself in Mark. Peter has just confessed him as the Christ (8:29).

decisions.choice: in name that you are Christ's, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: in my name, because you are Christ's
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "in my name". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: his reward: the giver's reward from God
decisions.reason: Even the smallest kindness to Christ's people is seen and rewarded by God.

decisions.choice: so much as; God will surely reward
alternatives: will by no means lose the reward
decisions.reason: Readable says the promise positively and names God as the one who rewards. "So much as" brings out how small the gift is.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} at every level
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese form of the christos setting, as in John.

decisions.choice: "người ấy ... của mình" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese words are already inclusive.

decisions.choice: {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} with the particle "에게" outside the span
decisions.reason: The Korean christos setting (style guide, section 7); both forms end in a vowel, so one particle fits both.

decisions.choice: "진실로 너희에게 말한다" stays in the middle of the sentence
alternatives: at the start of the sentence
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek order, with the solemn formula between the condition and the promise; Readable moves it to the front, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: de Cristo / del Mesías (L, B); a Cristo / al Mesías (R)
decisions.reason: Christos takes the christos setting; as elsewhere in the Spanish, the span includes the preposition so that the alternative can read "del Mesías" / "al Mesías".

decisions.choice: au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}
decisions.reason: French contracts "à" and the article into "au", which fits both options ("au Christ", "au Messie"), so the article stays outside the span at every level, where the English Balanced and Readable put "the Messiah" inside it.

decisions.choice: ninyi ni wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}
alternatives: the article with Christ, as the English Literal has it
decisions.reason: Swahili has no article, so where the English Literal writes "the Christ" every Swahili level has the plain span, which reads naturally with either wording.

decisions.choice: {{christos:de Cristo|do Messias}} (L); {{christos:a Cristo|ao Messias}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Cristo" stands without an article as a name, "Messias" needs one, so the preposition goes inside both options of the span (as docs/portuguese-style.md, section 7, does for the divine name).

decisions.choice: perderá a sua recompensa, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: Portuguese needs no subject pronoun after "quem", which already means anyone, so the English gender spans have no counterpart.

source.text: Καὶ ὃς ἂν σκανδαλίσῃ ἕνα τῶν μικρῶν τούτων τῶν πιστευόντων εἰς ἐμέ, καλόν ἐστιν αὐτῷ μᾶλλον εἰ περίκειται μύλος ὀνικὸς περὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ βέβληται εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν.

records.literal_gloss: And whoever might cause to stumble one of the little ones these, the believing in me, better it is for him rather if is put a millstone of a donkey around the neck of him and he has been cast into the sea.

en.L: And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to stumble, it is better for {{gender:them|him}} if a donkey's millstone is put around {{gender:their|his}} neck and {{gender:they are|he is}} thrown into the sea.
en.B: Whoever makes one of these little ones who believe in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} fall away would be better off having a huge millstone hung around the neck and being thrown into the sea.
en.R: Suppose someone leads one of these little ones who believe in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} into sin. It would be better for that person to have a heavy stone for grinding grain tied around the neck and be thrown into the sea.

vi.L: Và ai làm cho một trong những người bé mọn này, là những người tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, vấp ngã, thì thà người ấy bị buộc cối đá [do] lừa [kéo] vào cổ và bị ném xuống biển còn tốt hơn.
vi.B: Ai làm cho một trong những người bé mọn này, là những người tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, phải sa ngã, thì thà người ấy bị đeo một cối đá lớn vào cổ mà ném xuống biển còn hơn.
vi.R: Giả sử có ai đó khiến một người trong những người bé nhỏ tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} này phạm tội. Thì thà người ấy bị buộc một tảng đá nặng dùng để xay lúa vào cổ rồi bị ném xuống biển còn tốt hơn.

ko.L: 그리고 누구든지 나를 믿는 이 작은 사람들 가운데 하나를 걸려 넘어지게 하면, 차라리 그 사람의 목에 연자 맷돌이 매여 바다에 던져지는 것이 그에게 더 낫다.
ko.B: 누구든지 나를 믿는 이 작은 사람들 가운데 하나라도 죄짓게 하는 사람은, 차라리 큰 맷돌을 목에 매달고 바다에 던져지는 편이 더 낫다.
ko.R: 나를 믿는 이 작은 사람들 가운데 하나라도 죄를 짓게 만드는 사람이 있다고 하자. 그런 사람은 곡식을 가는 무거운 돌을 목에 매달고 바다에 던져지는 것이 더 낫다.

es.L: Y a cualquiera que haga tropezar a uno de estos pequeños que creen en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, mejor le es que se le ponga al cuello una piedra de molino de asno y sea arrojado al mar.
es.B: Al que haga caer a uno de estos pequeños que creen en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, más le valdría que le colgaran al cuello una enorme piedra de molino y lo arrojaran al mar.
es.R: Supongamos que alguien hace pecar a uno de estos pequeños que creen en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Sería mejor para esa persona que le ataran al cuello una piedra grande de moler grano y la tiraran al mar.

fr.L: Et quiconque fait trébucher un de ces petits qui croient en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, il vaut mieux pour lui qu’une meule [tournée par un] âne soit placée autour de son cou et qu’il soit jeté dans la mer.
fr.B: Celui qui fait tomber un de ces petits qui croient en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, il vaudrait mieux pour lui qu’on lui attache au cou une grosse meule de moulin et qu’on le jette à la mer.
fr.R: Imaginez quelqu’un qui pousse au péché un de ces petits qui croient en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Il vaudrait mieux pour lui qu’on lui attache au cou une lourde pierre à moudre le grain et qu’on le jette dans la mer.

sw.L: Na yeyote atakayemkwaza mmoja wa wadogo hawa wanaoniamini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, ni afadhali kwake kama jiwe la kusagia linalozungushwa na punda likifungwa shingoni mwake, naye akatupwa baharini.
sw.B: Mtu yeyote atakayemfanya mmoja wa wadogo hawa wanaoniamini aiache imani, ingekuwa afadhali kwake kufungiwa jiwe kubwa la kusagia shingoni na kutupwa baharini.
sw.R: Tuseme mtu fulani anamfanya mmoja wa wadogo hawa wanaoniamini atende dhambi. Ingekuwa afadhali kwa mtu huyo kufungiwa shingoni jiwe zito la kusagia nafaka, na kutupwa baharini.

pt.L: E quem fizer tropeçar um destes pequeninos que creem em {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, melhor lhe seria que lhe pusessem uma mó de jumento em volta do pescoço e ele fosse lançado ao mar.
pt.B: Se alguém levar a pecar um destes pequeninos que creem em {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, seria melhor para essa pessoa ser jogada no mar com uma grande pedra de moinho pendurada no pescoço.
pt.R: Se alguém levar um destes pequeninos que acreditam em {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} a pecar, seria melhor para essa pessoa ser jogada no mar com uma pedra pesada de moer grãos amarrada no pescoço.

decisions.choice: cause to stumble: cause to fall into sin or away from faith
decisions.reason: The verb means to trip someone up. In Mark it is used of falling away (4:17; 14:27).

decisions.choice: a donkey's millstone: the large upper stone of a mill turned by a donkey
decisions.reason: The word describes a millstone so heavy that an animal was needed to turn it. A man with one around his neck would sink at once.

decisions.choice: these little ones who believe in me: humble believers, like the child of 9:36
decisions.reason: "Little ones" follows the child Jesus held, but "who believe in me" shows that his followers are meant, however small.

decisions.choice: in me, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts lack "in me". The SBLGNT includes it. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: fall away (B); sin (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the stumbling is.

decisions.choice: a heavy stone for grinding grain
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a millstone is.

decisions.choice: "vấp ngã" (L), "sa ngã" (B), "phạm tội" (R) for "cause to stumble"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of stumbling; Balanced and Readable say where the stumbling leads. The same in 9:43-47.

decisions.choice: "cối đá [do] lừa [kéo]" (a donkey's millstone)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese needs the verb to say how the donkey belongs to the millstone.

decisions.choice: "걸려 넘어지게 하다" (L); "죄짓게 하다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: To cause to stumble is to cause to fall into sin or away from faith (meaning decision); Literal keeps the picture, Balanced and Readable say what it means. "실족" is the older church word.

decisions.choice: "연자 맷돌" (L); "큰 맷돌" (B)
decisions.reason: A "연자 맷돌" is the Korean name for a large millstone turned by an animal, which is what the donkey's millstone was (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: hacer tropezar (L); hacer caer (B); hacer pecar (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps the picture of stumbling; Balanced and Readable say where the stumbling leads (meaning decision). The same pattern runs through 9:43-47.

decisions.choice: faire trébucher (L); faire tomber (B); pousser au péché (R); in 9:43-47 te fait trébucher (L), t’entraîne à pécher (B), te fait pécher (R)
decisions.reason: French "scandaliser" now means "shock", not "cause to fall". Literal keeps the picture of stumbling; Balanced and Readable say what it leads to, as the English does.

decisions.choice: une meule [tournée par un] âne (L)
decisions.reason: "Une meule d’âne" is not clear French; the bracketed words say what the Greek phrase means (meaning decision on the donkey’s millstone).

decisions.choice: kukwaza (L); kufanya aiache imani (B); kufanya atende dhambi (R)
decisions.reason: "Kukwaza" is to make someone stumble, the picture of the Greek word, at Literal here and in 9:43-47. Balanced and Readable say what the stumbling is, as the English does: falling away from faith (B), being led into sin (R). In 9:43-47 Balanced says "kukuangusha dhambini" (make you fall into sin).

decisions.choice: lhe ... ele, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The pronouns refer back to "quem", whoever; Portuguese reads the "lhe" and "ele" that follow it as generic, so no setting is needed (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 7). Balanced and Readable say "essa pessoa", as the English does.

decisions.choice: uma mó de jumento
decisions.reason: As Matthew 18:6: Literal keeps the Greek's "donkey's millstone" (m2); Balanced says "uma grande pedra de moinho", Readable explains what it is.

source.text: Καὶ ἐὰν σκανδαλίζῃ σε ἡ χείρ σου, ἀπόκοψον αὐτήν· καλόν ἐστίν σε κυλλὸν εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν ζωὴν ἢ τὰς δύο χεῖρας ἔχοντα ἀπελθεῖν εἰς τὴν γέενναν, εἰς τὸ πῦρ τὸ ἄσβεστον.

records.literal_gloss: And if causes to stumble you the hand of you, cut off it; better it is for you maimed to enter into the life than the two hands having to go away into the Gehenna, into the fire the unquenchable.

en.L: And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off; it is better for you to enter into life maimed than having two hands to go away into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire.
en.B: If your hand leads you into sin, cut it off. You are better off entering life maimed than going off with both hands into hell, into the fire that cannot be put out.
en.R: If your hand makes you sin, cut it off. It is better to have only one hand and enter into life with God than to keep both hands and go to hell. Hell is the place where the fire never goes out.

vi.L: Và nếu tay con làm cho con vấp ngã, hãy chặt nó đi; con bị tàn tật mà vào sự sống thì tốt hơn là có đủ hai tay mà đi vào Ghê-hen-na, vào lửa không hề tắt.
vi.B: Nếu tay con khiến con sa ngã, hãy chặt nó đi. Thà con bị cụt tay mà vào sự sống, còn hơn là có đủ hai tay mà đi vào địa ngục, vào lửa không bao giờ tắt.
vi.R: Nếu tay con khiến con phạm tội, hãy chặt nó đi. Thà con chỉ còn một tay mà vào sự sống với Đức Chúa Trời, còn hơn là giữ cả hai tay mà phải vào địa ngục. Địa ngục là nơi lửa không bao giờ tắt.

ko.L: 그리고 만일 네 손이 너를 걸려 넘어지게 하면, 그것을 잘라 버려라. 두 손을 가지고 게헨나, 곧 꺼지지 않는 불에 들어가는 것보다, 불구가 되어 생명에 들어가는 것이 네게 더 낫다.
ko.B: 네 손이 너를 죄짓게 하면, 그 손을 잘라 버려라. 두 손을 가지고 지옥, 곧 꺼지지 않는 불에 들어가는 것보다, 장애를 입은 몸으로 생명에 들어가는 것이 더 낫다.
ko.R: 네 손이 너를 죄짓게 하면, 그 손을 잘라 버려라. 두 손을 다 가지고 지옥에 가는 것보다, 한 손만 가지고 하나님과 함께하는 생명에 들어가는 것이 더 낫다. 지옥은 불이 절대로 꺼지지 않는 곳이다.

es.L: Y si tu mano te hace tropezar, córtala; mejor te es entrar manco en la vida que, teniendo las dos manos, ir a la Gehena, al fuego inextinguible.
es.B: Si tu mano te hace caer en pecado, córtala. Más te vale entrar en la vida manco que ir con las dos manos al infierno, al fuego que no se puede apagar.
es.R: Si tu mano te hace pecar, córtatela. Es mejor tener una sola mano y entrar en la vida con Dios que tener las dos manos e ir al infierno. El infierno es el lugar donde el fuego nunca se apaga.

fr.L: Et si ta main te fait trébucher, coupe-la ; il est bon pour toi d’entrer dans la vie estropié plutôt que, ayant les deux mains, de t’en aller dans la Géhenne, dans le feu inextinguible.
fr.B: Si ta main t’entraîne à pécher, coupe-la. Mieux vaut pour toi entrer dans la vie mutilé que de t’en aller avec tes deux mains en enfer, dans le feu qui ne s’éteint pas.
fr.R: Si ta main te fait pécher, coupe-la. Il vaut mieux n’avoir qu’une main et entrer dans la vie avec Dieu que de garder tes deux mains et d’aller en enfer. L’enfer, c’est l’endroit où le feu ne s’éteint jamais.

sw.L: Na mkono wako ukikukwaza, ukate; ni afadhali wewe kuingia katika uzima ukiwa kilema, kuliko kuwa na mikono miwili na kwenda Jehanamu, katika moto usiozimika.
sw.B: Mkono wako ukikuangusha dhambini, ukate. Ni bora kwako kuingia katika uzima ukiwa na kilema, kuliko kwenda Jehanamu na mikono yako yote miwili, kwenye moto usioweza kuzimwa.
sw.R: Mkono wako ukikufanya utende dhambi, ukate. Ni afadhali kuwa na mkono mmoja tu na kuingia katika uzima pamoja na Mungu, kuliko kubaki na mikono yote miwili na kwenda Jehanamu. Jehanamu ni mahali ambapo moto hauzimiki kamwe.

pt.L: E, se a sua mão o faz tropeçar, corte-a; é melhor para você entrar na vida aleijado do que, tendo as duas mãos, ir para a geena, para o fogo inextinguível.
pt.B: Se a sua mão o leva a pecar, corte-a. É melhor entrar na vida mutilado do que ir com as duas mãos para o inferno, para o fogo que não se apaga.
pt.R: Se a sua mão faz você pecar, corte-a. É melhor ter uma mão só e entrar na vida com Deus do que ficar com as duas mãos e ir para o inferno. O inferno é o lugar onde o fogo nunca se apaga.

decisions.choice: Gehenna: the Valley of Hinnom, a name for the place of final judgment
decisions.reason: The Valley of Hinnom lay south of Jerusalem. Children had been burned there as sacrifices to idols (2 Kings 23:10; Jeremiah 7:31), and its name came to stand for the fire of God's judgment, as in Matthew 5:22.

decisions.choice: the unquenchable fire: fire that no one can put out
alternatives: a fire that burns for a while
decisions.reason: The fire of judgment cannot be stopped (Isaiah 66:24; Matthew 3:12).

decisions.choice: life: the life of the age to come
decisions.reason: "Life" here stands in parallel with "the kingdom of God" in 9:47.

decisions.choice: cut it off: get rid of whatever leads to sin, at any cost
decisions.reason: The picture is deliberately extreme. Losing a hand is better than losing everything.

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT has no verse 44
alternatives: add verse 44: where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add here the words of 9:48, which also follow 9:45 in those manuscripts (verse 46). The earliest manuscripts lack them, and scribes likely copied the line from 9:48 to make the three sayings match. Verse 44 is skipped in the numbering for this reason. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: Gehenna (L); hell (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the place name, as in Matthew 5:22. Balanced and Readable use the English word for the place of final judgment.

decisions.choice: life with God; Hell is the place where the fire never goes out
decisions.reason: Readable explains what life and hell mean here in short sentences.

decisions.choice: "Ghê-hen-na" (L); "địa ngục" (B, R) for Gehenna
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the place name as the English Literal does; "địa ngục" is the common Protestant word for the place of final judgment. The same in 9:45 and 9:47.

decisions.choice: singular "con" for the singular "you" of the sayings in 9:43-47
decisions.reason: The Greek turns to the singular, speaking to each disciple; "con" is how Jesus speaks to one disciple.

decisions.choice: "게헨나" (L); "지옥" (B, R), through chapter 9
decisions.reason: Gehenna is the name of the place of final judgment (meaning decision); Literal keeps the name, Balanced and Readable use the common Korean word, as the English does with "hell".

decisions.choice: "장애를 입은 몸으로"
decisions.reason: "불구" is kept at Literal for the Greek "maimed"; Balanced uses the respectful modern phrase, since older words for disability are now felt as insults.

decisions.choice: Gehena (L); infierno (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English, and as James 3:6 does in Spanish: Literal keeps the place name; Balanced and Readable use the ordinary word for the place of final judgment.

decisions.choice: Jehanamu at every level
decisions.reason: The English has Gehenna at Literal and hell at Balanced and Readable. "Jehanamu" is the Swahili form of the name Gehenna itself and the ordinary Swahili word for hell, so one word serves every level, as in James 3:6. "Kuzimu" is the world of the dead, not the place of judgment.

decisions.choice: uzima (life)
decisions.reason: As in John, "uzima" is life itself, the life of the age to come that the meaning decision describes; "maisha" would be a lifetime. The same in 9:45.

source.text: καὶ ἐὰν ὁ πούς σου σκανδαλίζῃ σε, ἀπόκοψον αὐτόν· καλόν ἐστίν σε εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν ζωὴν χωλὸν ἢ τοὺς δύο πόδας ἔχοντα βληθῆναι εἰς τὴν γέενναν.

records.literal_gloss: And if the foot of you causes to stumble you, cut off it; better it is for you to enter into the life lame than the two feet having to be cast into the Gehenna.

en.L: And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off; it is better for you to enter into life lame than having two feet to be thrown into Gehenna.
en.B: If your foot leads you into sin, cut it off. You are better off entering life lame than being thrown into hell with both feet.
en.R: If your foot makes you sin, cut it off. It is better to be lame and enter into life with God than to keep both feet and be thrown into hell.

vi.L: Và nếu chân con làm cho con vấp ngã, hãy chặt nó đi; con bị què mà vào sự sống thì tốt hơn là có đủ hai chân mà bị ném vào Ghê-hen-na.
vi.B: Nếu chân con khiến con sa ngã, hãy chặt nó đi. Thà con bị què mà vào sự sống, còn hơn là có đủ hai chân mà bị ném vào địa ngục.
vi.R: Nếu chân con khiến con phạm tội, hãy chặt nó đi. Thà con bị què mà vào sự sống với Đức Chúa Trời, còn hơn là giữ cả hai chân mà bị ném vào địa ngục.

ko.L: 그리고 만일 네 발이 너를 걸려 넘어지게 하면, 그것을 잘라 버려라. 두 발을 가지고 게헨나에 던져지는 것보다, 다리를 저는 채로 생명에 들어가는 것이 네게 더 낫다.
ko.B: 네 발이 너를 죄짓게 하면, 그 발을 잘라 버려라. 두 발을 가지고 지옥에 던져지는 것보다, 다리를 저는 몸으로 생명에 들어가는 것이 더 낫다.
ko.R: 네 발이 너를 죄짓게 하면, 그 발을 잘라 버려라. 두 발을 다 가지고 지옥에 던져지는 것보다, 다리를 절면서라도 하나님과 함께하는 생명에 들어가는 것이 더 낫다.

es.L: Y si tu pie te hace tropezar, córtalo; mejor te es entrar cojo en la vida que, teniendo los dos pies, ser arrojado a la Gehena.
es.B: Si tu pie te hace caer en pecado, córtalo. Más te vale entrar en la vida cojo que ser arrojado al infierno con los dos pies.
es.R: Si tu pie te hace pecar, córtatelo. Es mejor ser cojo y entrar en la vida con Dios que tener los dos pies y ser arrojado al infierno.

fr.L: Et si ton pied te fait trébucher, coupe-le ; il est bon pour toi d’entrer dans la vie boiteux plutôt que, ayant les deux pieds, d’être jeté dans la Géhenne.
fr.B: Si ton pied t’entraîne à pécher, coupe-le. Mieux vaut pour toi entrer dans la vie boiteux que d’être jeté en enfer avec tes deux pieds.
fr.R: Si ton pied te fait pécher, coupe-le. Il vaut mieux être boiteux et entrer dans la vie avec Dieu que de garder tes deux pieds et d’être jeté en enfer.

sw.L: Na mguu wako ukikukwaza, ukate; ni afadhali wewe kuingia katika uzima ukiwa kiwete, kuliko kuwa na miguu miwili na kutupwa Jehanamu.
sw.B: Mguu wako ukikuangusha dhambini, ukate. Ni bora kwako kuingia katika uzima ukiwa kiwete, kuliko kutupwa Jehanamu na miguu yako yote miwili.
sw.R: Mguu wako ukikufanya utende dhambi, ukate. Ni afadhali kuwa kiwete na kuingia katika uzima pamoja na Mungu, kuliko kubaki na miguu yote miwili na kutupwa Jehanamu.

pt.L: E, se o seu pé o faz tropeçar, corte-o; é melhor para você entrar na vida manco do que, tendo os dois pés, ser lançado na geena.
pt.B: Se o seu pé o leva a pecar, corte-o. É melhor entrar na vida manco do que ser lançado no inferno com os dois pés.
pt.R: Se o seu pé faz você pecar, corte-o. É melhor ser manco e entrar na vida com Deus do que ficar com os dois pés e ser jogado no inferno.

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT has no verse 46
alternatives: add verse 46: where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched
decisions.reason: As with verse 44, many later manuscripts repeat here the words of 9:48. The earliest manuscripts lack them, and they are likely a copy of 9:48. Verse 46 is skipped in the numbering for this reason. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: into Gehenna, the end of the saying in the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some later manuscripts add "into the unquenchable fire", as in 9:43. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: to be thrown: a passive, the judgment of God
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the actor unnamed. The one who judges is God.

decisions.choice: hell
decisions.reason: As in 9:43.

source.text: καὶ ἐὰν ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου σκανδαλίζῃ σε, ἔκβαλε αὐτόν· καλόν σέ ἐστιν μονόφθαλμον εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ ἢ δύο ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχοντα βληθῆναι εἰς τὴν γέενναν, ὅπου ὁ σκώληξ αὐτῶν οὐ τελευτᾷ καὶ τὸ πῦρ οὐ σβέννυται.

records.literal_gloss: And if the eye of you causes to stumble you, cast out it; better for you it is one-eyed to enter into the kingdom of God than two eyes having to be cast into the Gehenna, \v 48 where the worm of them not dies and the fire not is quenched.

en.L: And if your eye causes you to stumble, throw it out; it is better for you to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye than having two eyes to be thrown into Gehenna, \v 48 where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.
en.B: If your eye leads you into sin, tear it out. You are better off entering the kingdom of God with only one eye than being thrown into hell with two, \v 48 where the worm that eats them never dies and the fire is never put out.
en.R: If your eye makes you sin, take it out. It is better to have only one eye and enter the kingdom of God than to keep both eyes and be thrown into hell. \v 48 In that place the worms that eat people never die, and the fire never goes out.

vi.L: Và nếu mắt con làm cho con vấp ngã, hãy móc nó ra; con chỉ còn một mắt mà vào vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời thì tốt hơn là có đủ hai mắt mà bị ném vào Ghê-hen-na, \v 48 là nơi giòi của họ không chết và lửa không tắt.
vi.B: Nếu mắt con khiến con sa ngã, hãy móc nó ra. Thà con chỉ còn một mắt mà vào vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời, còn hơn là có đủ hai mắt mà bị ném vào địa ngục, \v 48 nơi giòi bọ ăn họ không bao giờ chết và lửa không bao giờ tắt.
vi.R: Nếu mắt con khiến con phạm tội, hãy móc bỏ nó đi. Thà con chỉ còn một mắt mà vào vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời, còn hơn là giữ cả hai mắt mà bị ném vào địa ngục. \v 48 Ở đó, giòi bọ ăn thịt người ta không bao giờ chết, và lửa không bao giờ tắt.

ko.L: 그리고 만일 네 눈이 너를 걸려 넘어지게 하면, 그것을 빼어 버려라. 두 눈을 가지고 게헨나에 던져지는 것보다, 한 눈으로 하나님의 나라에 들어가는 것이 네게 더 낫다. \v 48 그곳에서는 그들의 구더기도 죽지 않고, 불도 꺼지지 않는다.
ko.B: 네 눈이 너를 죄짓게 하면, 그 눈을 빼어 버려라. 두 눈을 가지고 지옥에 던져지는 것보다, 한 눈만 가지고 하나님의 나라에 들어가는 것이 더 낫다. \v 48 그곳에서는 그들을 먹는 구더기도 죽지 않고, 불도 꺼지지 않는다.
ko.R: 네 눈이 너를 죄짓게 하면, 그 눈을 빼 버려라. 두 눈을 다 가지고 지옥에 던져지는 것보다, 한 눈만 가지고 하나님의 나라에 들어가는 것이 더 낫다. \v 48 그곳에서는 사람을 먹는 구더기도 죽지 않고, 불도 영원히 꺼지지 않는다.

es.L: Y si tu ojo te hace tropezar, échalo fuera; mejor te es entrar con un solo ojo en el reino de Dios que, teniendo dos ojos, ser arrojado a la Gehena, \v 48 donde su gusano no muere y el fuego no se apaga.
es.B: Si tu ojo te hace caer en pecado, sácatelo. Más te vale entrar en el reino de Dios con un solo ojo que ser arrojado al infierno con los dos, \v 48 donde el gusano que los consume nunca muere y el fuego nunca se apaga.
es.R: Si tu ojo te hace pecar, sácatelo. Es mejor tener un solo ojo y entrar en el reino de Dios que tener los dos ojos y ser arrojado al infierno. \v 48 En ese lugar, los gusanos que comen a la gente nunca mueren, y el fuego nunca se apaga.

fr.L: Et si ton œil te fait trébucher, jette-le dehors ; il est bon pour toi d’entrer dans le royaume de Dieu avec un seul œil plutôt que, ayant deux yeux, d’être jeté dans la Géhenne, \v 48 où leur ver ne meurt pas et où le feu ne s’éteint pas.
fr.B: Si ton œil t’entraîne à pécher, arrache-le. Mieux vaut pour toi entrer dans le royaume de Dieu avec un seul œil que d’être jeté en enfer avec tes deux yeux, \v 48 là où le ver qui les ronge ne meurt jamais et où le feu ne s’éteint jamais.
fr.R: Si ton œil te fait pécher, enlève-le. Il vaut mieux n’avoir qu’un œil et entrer dans le royaume de Dieu que de garder tes deux yeux et d’être jeté en enfer. \v 48 Dans cet endroit, les vers qui mangent les gens ne meurent jamais, et le feu ne s’éteint jamais.

sw.L: Na jicho lako likikukwaza, ling'oe; ni afadhali wewe kuingia katika ufalme wa Mungu ukiwa na jicho moja, kuliko kuwa na macho mawili na kutupwa Jehanamu, \v 48 ambako funza wao hafi na moto hauzimiki.
sw.B: Jicho lako likikuangusha dhambini, ling'oe. Ni bora kwako kuingia katika ufalme wa Mungu ukiwa na jicho moja, kuliko kutupwa Jehanamu ukiwa na macho mawili, \v 48 ambako funza wanaowala hawafi kamwe, na moto hauzimwi kamwe.
sw.R: Jicho lako likikufanya utende dhambi, liondoe. Ni afadhali kuwa na jicho moja tu na kuingia katika ufalme wa Mungu, kuliko kubaki na macho yote mawili na kutupwa Jehanamu. \v 48 Mahali hapo funza wanaowala watu hawafi kamwe, na moto hauzimiki kamwe.

pt.L: E, se o seu olho o faz tropeçar, lance-o fora; é melhor para você entrar no Reino de Deus com um olho só do que, tendo dois olhos, ser lançado na geena, \v 48 onde o verme deles não morre e o fogo não se apaga.
pt.B: Se o seu olho o leva a pecar, arranque-o. É melhor entrar no Reino de Deus com um olho só do que ser lançado no inferno com os dois, \v 48 onde o verme que os devora nunca morre e o fogo nunca se apaga.
pt.R: Se o seu olho faz você pecar, tire-o. É melhor ter um olho só e entrar no Reino de Deus do que ficar com os dois olhos e ser jogado no inferno. \v 48 Nesse lugar, os vermes que comem as pessoas nunca morrem, e o fogo nunca se apaga.

decisions.choice: their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched: the last verse of Isaiah
decisions.reason: Isaiah 66:24 describes the dead bodies of those who rebelled against God, eaten by worms and burned by fire that never ends.

decisions.choice: throw it out: the same verb as casting out demons
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the strong verb for driving out: get rid of it.

decisions.choice: the kingdom of God: the same as life in 9:43 and 9:45
decisions.reason: The three sayings set "life" and "the kingdom of God" side by side as the same goal.

decisions.choice: their worm: the worm that feeds on those thrown there
alternatives: the worm that belongs to them as a pet
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to the people in Gehenna.

decisions.choice: tear it out (B); take it out (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a verb that fits an eye. Literal keeps "throw out".

decisions.choice: hell
decisions.reason: As in 9:43.

decisions.choice: "móc ... ra" for "throw it out"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese needs a verb that fits an eye; the link with "đuổi ra" (casting out) that the meaning decision notes cannot be kept.

decisions.choice: "구더기"
decisions.reason: The worm feeds on the bodies of those thrown there (meaning decision); "구더기" is the Korean word for such a worm, where "벌레" is any insect.

decisions.choice: échalo fuera (L); sácatelo (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the wording that matches casting out demons (meaning decision); Balanced and Readable use the natural Spanish for removing an eye.

decisions.choice: everyone will be salted with fire, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: add: and every sacrifice will be salted with salt
every sacrifice will be salted with salt (in place of the saying)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "and every sacrifice will be salted with salt", and some have that line instead. It comes from Leviticus 2:13, where every grain offering was to be seasoned with salt, and was likely added by scribes to explain the saying. The earliest manuscripts have only the shorter text. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: salted with fire: everyone will be tested and purified, as a sacrifice is salted
alternatives: the wicked will be kept in the fire of judgment
disciples will be refined by suffering
decisions.reason: The saying is one of the hardest in Mark. "For" links it to the fire of 9:48. It may mean that every disciple will be made pure through trial, as offerings were salted (Leviticus 2:13). It may also mean that those in judgment are preserved in the fire. Mark does not explain it.

decisions.choice: for: the saying explains what came before
decisions.reason: The word ties the salt to the fire of the previous saying.

decisions.choice: Every person will be salted with fire
alternatives: everyone will be purified by fire
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture rather than choose one explanation, because the meaning is uncertain.

decisions.choice: "được ướp muối" (salted), with the neutral "được"
decisions.reason: "bị" would make the saying only a punishment; "được" fits the meaning decision that reads it as testing and purifying, as salt is put on a sacrifice. The sense is disputed.

decisions.choice: "소금 쳐지다" (L); "소금 침을 받다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The saying is obscure (meaning decision, footnoted) and every level keeps its picture of salting as a sacrifice is salted; Korean says to salt with "소금을 치다", and the passive is made with "받다" at Balanced and Readable.

records.literal_gloss: Good [is] the salt; if however the salt unsalty becomes, with what it will you season?

en.L: Salt [is] good; but if the salt becomes unsalty, with what will you season it?
en.B: Salt is a good thing. But if the salt stops being salty, how will you give it back its flavor?
en.R: Salt is good. But if salt loses its taste, nothing can make it salty again.

vi.L: Muối [là] tốt; nhưng nếu muối trở nên nhạt, các con sẽ lấy gì mà làm cho nó mặn lại?
vi.B: Muối là vật tốt. Nhưng nếu muối mất vị mặn thì các con lấy gì làm cho nó mặn lại?
vi.R: Muối là tốt. Nhưng nếu muối mất vị mặn, thì không có gì làm cho nó mặn lại được.

ko.L: 소금은 좋은 것이다. 그러나 소금이 짠맛을 잃으면, 너희가 무엇으로 그것을 짜게 하겠느냐?
ko.B: 소금은 좋은 것이다. 그러나 소금이 짠맛을 잃으면, 무엇으로 그 맛을 되살리겠느냐?
ko.R: 소금은 좋은 것이다. 그러나 소금이 짠맛을 잃으면, 아무것도 그것을 다시 짜게 만들 수 없다.

es.L: Buena [es] la sal; pero si la sal se vuelve insípida, ¿con qué la {{plural_you:sazonarán|sazonaréis}}?
es.B: La sal es buena. Pero si la sal deja de ser salada, ¿cómo le {{plural_you:devolverán|devolveréis}} el sabor?
es.R: La sal es buena. Pero si la sal pierde su sabor, nada puede hacer que vuelva a ser salada.

fr.L: Le sel [est] bon ; mais si le sel devient sans saveur, avec quoi l’assaisonnerez-vous ?
fr.B: Le sel est une bonne chose. Mais si le sel perd son goût salé, comment lui rendrez-vous sa saveur ?
fr.R: Le sel, c’est bon. Mais si le sel perd son goût, rien ne peut le rendre salé de nouveau.

sw.L: Chumvi ni nzuri; lakini chumvi ikiacha kuwa na chumvi, mtaikoleza kwa nini?
sw.B: Chumvi ni kitu kizuri. Lakini chumvi ikipoteza ukali wake, mtairudishiaje ladha yake?
sw.R: Chumvi ni nzuri. Lakini chumvi ikipoteza ladha yake, hakuna kinachoweza kuifanya iwe na chumvi tena.

pt.L: O sal [é] bom; mas, se o sal ficar insosso, com que vocês o temperarão?
pt.B: O sal é uma coisa boa. Mas, se o sal perder o sabor, como vocês vão devolver o gosto a ele?
pt.R: O sal é bom. Mas, se o sal perder o gosto, não há nada que o faça ficar salgado de novo.

decisions.choice: salt becomes unsalty: impure salt could lose its taste
decisions.reason: Salt gathered from the Dead Sea was mixed with other minerals. When the salt was washed out by damp, what was left looked like salt but had no taste.

decisions.choice: with what will you season it: a question expecting the answer, nothing
alternatives: a real request for a method
decisions.reason: Salt that has lost its taste cannot be restored.

decisions.choice: season: give it flavor
decisions.reason: The verb means to season food.

decisions.choice: nothing can make it salty again
alternatives: with what will you season it?
decisions.reason: Readable gives the answer the question expects.

pt.R: Guardem o sal na vida de vocês e vivam em paz uns com os outros."

decisions.choice: in yourselves: within each of you, or among you as a group
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean in each person or among the company. With "one another" following, both may be in view.

decisions.choice: salt: the mark of a true disciple, perhaps also of a covenant shared
decisions.reason: Salt was part of God's covenant with Israel (Leviticus 2:13; Numbers 18:19), and sharing salt meant friendship. The call to be at peace answers the quarrel about greatness (9:34).

decisions.choice: be at peace: live in peace, the verb form of peace
decisions.reason: The verb is about relations between people.

decisions.choice: in your lives
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain phrase that keeps the open sense.

decisions.choice: "sống hòa thuận" for "be at peace with one another"
decisions.reason: "bình an" stays for the noun peace; for peace between people Vietnamese says "hòa thuận".

decisions.choice: "화평하게 지내다" (L, B); "사이좋게 지내다" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb here is peace between people, living at peace with one another (meaning decision); "평안" in the Korean John is the peace Jesus gives (14:27), so the verb takes the word Korean uses for peace in relationships.
